verses.1:1: Now it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David had returned from striking down Amalek, that David remained in Ziklag two days.
verses.1:2: And it came to pass on the third day that, behold, a man came from the camp, from the people of Saul, with his garments torn and earth upon his head. And when he came in to David, he fell to the ground and bowed down before him.
verses.1:3: And David said to him, "Where have you come from?" And he said to him, "I have escaped from the camp of Israel."
verses.1:4: Then David said to him, "What is this matter? Tell me." And he answered, "The people have fled from the battle, and many of the people have fallen and died; and Saul also has died, and Jonathan his son has died."
verses.1:5: And David said to the young man who brought him the report, "How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?"
verses.1:6: Then the young man who reported to him said, "By chance I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and behold, Saul was leaning upon his spear; and behold, the chariots and the commanders of the horsemen were closing in on him.
verses.1:7: And he looked behind him, and saw me and called me; and I said, 'Here I am.'
verses.1:8: And he said to me, 'Who are you?' And I answered, 'I am an Amalekite.'
verses.1:9: And he said to me, 'Stand over me now and put me to death, for a dreadful darkness has seized me, for all my life is still in me.'
verses.1:10: So I stood over him and put him to death, because I knew that he would not live after he had fallen. And I took the crown that was on his head and the armlet that was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord."
verses.1:11: Then David took hold of his own garments and tore them, and all the men who were with him tore their garments.
verses.1:12: And they mourned and fasted and wept until evening for Saul and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of Judah and for the house of Israel, because they had been struck down by the sword.
verses.1:13: Then David said to the young man who had brought him the report, "Where are you from?" And he answered, "I am the son of an Amalekite sojourner."
verses.1:14: And David said to him, "How were you not afraid to put forth your hand to destroy the anointed of the Lord?"
verses.1:15: Then David called one of his young men and said, "Draw near and fall upon him!" And he struck him, and he died.
verses.1:16: And David said to him, "Your blood be upon your own head, for your own mouth has testified against you, saying, 'I have put to death the anointed of the Lord.'"
verses.1:17: Then David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son,
verses.1:18: and he gave word to teach it to the sons of Judah; behold, it is written in the Book of the Upright:
verses.1:19: "Set up a monument, O Israel, for those who have died, slain upon your high places! How the mighty have fallen!
verses.1:20: Do not declare it in Gath, and do not proclaim good tidings in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the foreigners rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
verses.1:21: O mountains that are in Gilboa, let neither dew nor rain descend upon you, nor fields of firstfruits; for there the shield of the mighty was despised—the shield of Saul was not anointed with oil.
verses.1:22: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not turn back empty, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.
verses.1:23: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and fair, were not parted; comely in their life, and in their death they were not separated. They were swifter than eagles, and they were mightier than lions.
verses.1:24: O daughters of Israel, weep over Saul—weep for him who clothed you in scarlet with your adornment, who placed ornaments of gold upon your garments.
verses.1:25: How the mighty have fallen in the midst of the battle! O Jonathan, upon your high places lie the slain!
verses.1:26: I grieve for you, my brother Jonathan; you were exceedingly pleasant to me. Your love to me was wondrous, surpassing the love of women.
verses.1:27: How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!"
verses.2:1: Now it came to pass after these things that David inquired of the Lord, saying, "Shall I go up to one of the cities of Judah?" And the Lord said to him, "Go up." And David said, "Where shall I go up?" And He said, "To Hebron."
verses.2:2: So David went up there to Hebron, along with both his wives, Ahinoam the Israelitess and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite,
verses.2:3: and the men who were with him, each man and his household; and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.
verses.2:4: Then men of Judea came and anointed David there to reign over the house of Judah. And they reported to David, saying that the men of Jabesh of Gilead had buried Saul.
verses.2:5: So David sent messengers to the leaders of Jabesh of Gilead and said to them, "Blessed are you by the Lord, because you have shown the mercy of God to your lord Saul and have buried him.
verses.2:6: And now may the Lord show mercy and truth to you; and I also will do this good thing for you, because you have done this thing.
verses.2:7: Therefore now let your hands be strengthened, and be sons of valor; for your lord Saul is dead, and moreover the house of Judah has anointed me king over them."
verses.2:8: Now Abner the son of Ner, commander of Saul's army, took Ishbosheth the son of Saul and brought him up from the camp to Mahanaim,
verses.2:9: and he made him king over Gilead, and over Thasiri, and over Israel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
verses.2:10: Ishbosheth the son of Saul was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned two years, except for the house of Judah, who followed after David.
verses.2:11: And the days that David reigned in Hebron over the house of Judah were seven years and six months.
verses.2:12: Now Abner the son of Ner and the servants of Ishbosheth the son of Saul went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
verses.2:13: And Joab the son of Zeruiah and the servants of David went out from Hebron and met them together at the pool of Gibeon; and one side sat down at the pool of Gibeon on this side, and the other at the pool on that side.
verses.2:14: Then Abner said to Joab, "Let the young men now arise and make sport before us." And Joab said, "Let them arise."
verses.2:15: So they arose and came forward by number: twelve of the servants of Benjamin belonging to Ishbosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.
verses.2:16: And each man seized his opponent's head with his hand and drove his sword into his opponent's side, and they fell down together. Therefore the name of that place was called the Portion of the Plotters, which is in Gibeon.
verses.2:17: And the battle was exceedingly fierce on that day, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated before the servants of David.
verses.2:18: Now the three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. And Asahel was swift of foot, like a gazelle in the field.
verses.2:19: And Asahel pursued after Abner, and did not turn aside to go to the right or to the left from following Abner.
verses.2:20: Then Abner looked behind him and said, "Are you yourself Asahel?" And he answered, "I am."
verses.2:21: And Abner said to him, "Turn aside to the right or to the left, and lay hold of one of the young men for yourself and take his armor for yourself." Yet Asahel would not turn aside from following him.
verses.2:22: So Abner spoke yet again to Asahel, saying, "Turn away from me, lest I strike you down to the ground! And how then shall I lift up my face to Joab?
verses.2:23: And where do these things lead? Turn back to Joab your brother!" Yet he refused to turn away. Therefore Abner struck him in the loin with the butt end of the spear, so that the spear came out behind him; and he fell there and died on the spot. And it came to pass that everyone who came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died stood still.
verses.2:24: Joab and Abishai also pursued after Abner; and the sun was going down when they came to the hill of Amman, which is in front of Gai, by the wilderness way of Gibeon.
verses.2:25: And the sons of Benjamin who followed Abner gathered together, and formed one company, and took their stand on the top of a single hill.
verses.2:26: Then Abner called to Joab and said, "Shall the sword devour forever? Or do you not know that it will be bitter in the end? How long then will it be before you tell the people to turn back from pursuing our brethren?"
verses.2:27: And Joab said, "As the Lord lives, if you had not spoken, surely then from the morning the people would have gone up, each man following after his brother."
verses.2:28: So Joab blew the trumpet, and all the people halted and did not pursue after Israel, nor did they continue to fight any longer.
verses.2:29: And Abner and his men departed toward the west all that night, and crossed over the Jordan, and marched through all the adjoining region, and came to the camp.
verses.2:30: And Joab returned from pursuing Abner; and when he had gathered all the people together, nineteen men of the servants of David were missing,
verses.2:31: and Asahel. And the servants of David had struck down of the sons of Benjamin, of the men of Abner, three hundred and sixty men of his.
verses.2:32: Then they took up Asahel and buried him in the tomb of his father in Bethlehem. And Joab and the men who were with him marched all night, and the day dawned upon them at Hebron.
verses.3:1: Now the war lasted for a long time between the house of Saul and the house of David; and the house of David went on and grew stronger, and the house of Saul went on and grew weaker.
verses.3:2: And sons were born to David in Hebron: his firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam the Israelitess;
verses.3:3: and his second, Daluia, by Abigail the Carmelitess; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah, the daughter of Thommei, king of Geshur;
verses.3:4: and the fourth, Orneil the son of Pheggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah, by Abital;
verses.3:5: and the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah, David's wife. These were born to David in Hebron.
verses.3:6: And it came to pass, while the war was between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner was holding sway over the house of Saul.
verses.3:7: Now Saul had a concubine, Rizpah the daughter of Ial; and Mephibosheth the son of Saul said to Abner, "Why have you gone in to my father's concubine?"
verses.3:8: Then Abner was exceedingly angry at the word of Mephibosheth, and Abner said to him, "Am I a dog's head? Today I have shown mercy to the house of Saul your father, and to brethren and acquaintances, and I have not deserted to the house of David; and yet today you call me to account concerning the wrongdoing of a woman?
verses.3:9: May God do thus to Abner, and add more also to him, for just as the Lord swore to David, so indeed I will do for him on this day:
verses.3:10: to take away the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan to Beersheba."
verses.3:11: And Mephibosheth was no longer able to answer Abner a word, because he feared him.
verses.3:12: Then Abner sent messengers at once to David at Thailam, where he was, saying, "Make your covenant with me, and behold, my hand is with you to turn all the house of Israel back to you."
verses.3:13: And David said, "Good, I will make a covenant with you; yet one thing I ask of you, saying, 'You shall not see my face unless you bring Michal, the daughter of Saul, when you come to see my face.'"
verses.3:14: Then David sent messengers to Mephibosheth the son of Saul, saying, "Restore to me my wife Michal, whom I took for one hundred foreskins of the foreigners."
verses.3:15: And Mephibosheth sent and took her from her husband, from Paltiel the son of Selles.
verses.3:16: And her husband went along with her, weeping behind her as far as Barakei. Then Abner said to him, "Go, turn back." And he turned back.
verses.3:17: Now Abner spoke to the elders of Israel, saying, "In times past you sought David to reign over you.
verses.3:18: Now therefore do it, for the Lord has spoken concerning David, saying, 'By the hand of My servant David I will save Israel from the hand of the foreigners and from the hand of all their enemies.'"
verses.3:19: And Abner spoke in the ears of Benjamin; and Abner went to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that was pleasing in the eyes of Israel and in the eyes of the whole house of Benjamin.
verses.3:20: So Abner came to David in Hebron, and twenty men with him; and David made a feast for Abner and for the men who were with him.
verses.3:21: And Abner said to David, "I will arise now and go, and I will gather all Israel to my lord the king, and I will make a covenant with him, and you shall reign over all that your soul desires." So David sent Abner away, and they departed in peace.
verses.3:22: And behold, the servants of David and Joab arrived from the raid, and they brought much spoil with them; but Abner was not with David in Hebron, for he had sent him away, and he had departed in peace.
verses.3:23: And Joab and all his army arrived, and it was reported to Joab, saying, "Abner the son of Ner came to David, and he has sent him away, and he has departed in peace."
verses.3:24: Then Joab went in to the king and said, "What is this that you have done? Behold, Abner came to you; why then have you sent him away, and he has departed in peace?
verses.3:25: Or do you not know the malice of Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive you, and to know your going out and your coming in, and to know all that you do?"
verses.3:26: And Joab withdrew from David and sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the well of Seeiram; but David did not know it.
verses.3:27: And he brought Abner back to Hebron, and Joab drew him aside to the side of the gate to speak to him, lying in wait; and he struck him there in the loin, and he died for the blood of Asahel, the brother of Joab.
verses.3:28: And David heard of it afterward and said, "I and my kingdom are guiltless before the Lord even forever of the blood of Abner the son of Ner.
verses.3:29: Let it fall upon the head of Joab and upon all his father's house; and let there not fail from the house of Joab one who has a discharge, or a leper, or one who holds a staff, or one who falls by the sword, or one who lacks bread."
verses.3:30: Now Joab and Abishai his brother were lying in wait for Abner, because he had put to death Asahel their brother at Gibeon in the battle.
verses.3:31: Then David said to Joab and to all the people who were with him, "Tear your garments, gird yourselves with sackcloth, and mourn before Abner." And King David walked behind the bier.
verses.3:32: So they buried Abner in Hebron; and the king lifted up his voice and wept at his grave, and all the people wept over Abner.
verses.3:33: And the king lamented over Abner and said, "Should Abner die according to the death of Nabal?
verses.3:34: Your hands were not bound, your feet were not in fetters; he did not draw near like Nabal; before sons of unrighteousness you fell." And all the people were gathered together to weep for him.
verses.3:35: And all the people came to share a funeral meal of bread with David while it was still day; but David swore, saying, "May God do thus to me, and add more also, for until the sun goes down I will by no means taste bread or anything at all."
verses.3:36: And all the people took note of it, and all that the king did before the people was pleasing in their sight.
verses.3:37: So all the people and all Israel knew on that day that it had not been from the king to put Abner the son of Ner to death.
verses.3:38: And the king said to his servants, "Do you not know that a great leader has fallen on this day in Israel?
verses.3:39: And that today I am a kinsman and appointed by a king? Yet these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too harsh for me. May the Lord repay the one who does evil according to his wickedness."
verses.4:1: Now Mephibosheth the son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, and his hands became feeble, and all the men of Israel grew faint.
verses.4:2: And Mephibosheth the son of Saul had two men who were leaders of raiding bands: the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the second was Rechab, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the sons of Benjamin; for Beeroth was reckoned to the sons of Benjamin.
verses.4:3: And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and have been sojourning there to this day.
verses.4:4: Now Jonathan the son of Saul had a son who was stricken in his feet. He was five years old when the report of Saul and Jonathan his son came from Israel; and his nurse took him up and fled. And it came to pass, as he hastened to flee, that he fell and became lame; and his name was Mephibosheth.
verses.4:5: Then the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went and came in the heat of the day to the house of Mephibosheth, while he was sleeping on his bed at midday.
verses.4:6: And behold, the doorkeeper of the house was cleaning wheat, and she grew drowsy and fell asleep; so Rechab and Baanah the brothers slipped past unnoticed,
verses.4:7: and they entered the house, while Mephibosheth was sleeping on his bed in his bedchamber; and they struck him and put him to death, and removed his head. And they took his head and went by the way toward the west all night long.
verses.4:8: And they brought the head of Mephibosheth to David in Hebron, and said to the king, "Behold, the head of Mephibosheth, the son of Saul your enemy, who sought your life! And the Lord has given to the lord king vengeance on his enemies as on this day, from Saul your enemy and from his seed."
verses.4:9: But David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, "As the Lord lives, who has redeemed my soul from all affliction, as for the one who told me that Saul was dead,
verses.4:10: and he was as one bringing good tidings before me, I seized him and slew him in Ziklag, to whom I ought to have given a reward for good tidings.
verses.4:11: And now wicked men have slain a righteous man in his own house upon his bed! Now therefore I will require his blood from your hand, and I will utterly destroy you from the earth."
verses.4:12: Then David commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them by the spring in Hebron. And they buried the head of Mephibosheth in the tomb of Abner the son of Ner.
verses.5:1: And all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said to him, "Behold, we are your bones and your flesh.
verses.5:2: And in times past, when Saul was king over us, you were the one who led out and brought in Israel; and the Lord said to you, 'You shall shepherd My people Israel, and you shall be leader over Israel.'"
verses.5:3: And all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the Lord; and they anointed David as king over all Israel.
verses.5:4: David was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years:
verses.5:5: Seven years and six months he reigned in Hebron over Judah, and thirty-three years he reigned over all Israel and Judah in Jerusalem.
verses.5:6: And David and his men went to Jerusalem to the Jebusite who dwelt in the land; and it was said to David, "You shall not enter here," for the blind and the lame stood in opposition, saying, "David shall not enter here."
verses.5:7: And David captured the stronghold of Zion; this is the City of David.
verses.5:8: And David said on that day, "Whoever strikes a Jebusite, let him attack with a dagger both the lame and the blind, and those who hate the soul of David." Therefore they shall say, "The blind and the lame shall not enter the house of the Lord."
verses.5:9: And David dwelt in the stronghold, and it was called the City of David; and he built it as a city all around from the citadel, and also his own house.
verses.5:10: And David continued advancing and growing great, and the Lord Almighty was with him.
verses.5:11: And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar timber, and workers in wood and workers in stone, and they built a house for David.
verses.5:12: And David knew that the Lord had prepared him as king over Israel, and that his kingdom was exalted for the sake of His people Israel.
verses.5:13: And David took more wives and concubines from Jerusalem after he came to Hebron; and more sons and daughters were born to David.
verses.5:14: And these are the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Sammus, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon,
verses.5:15: and Ebear, and Elisus, and Naphek, and Jephies,
verses.5:16: and Elishama, and Epidae, and Eliphaath, Samae, Jessibath, Nathan, Galamaan, Jebaar, Theesus, Elphalat, Naged, Naphek, Janatha, Leasamys, Baalimath, Eliphaath.
verses.5:17: And the foreigners heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, and all the foreigners went up to seek David; and David heard of it, and went down to the stronghold.
verses.5:18: And the foreigners came and converged in the Valley of the Titans.
verses.5:19: And David inquired through the Lord, saying, "Shall I go up against the foreigners, and will You deliver them into my hands?" And the Lord said to David, "Go up, for I will surely deliver the foreigners into your hands."
verses.5:20: And David came from Upper Breaches and struck down the foreigners there; and David said, "The Lord has broken through the foreign enemies before me, as waters break through." Therefore the name of that place was called Upper Breaches.
verses.5:21: And they left their gods behind there, and David and the men who were with him took them.
verses.5:22: And the foreigners went up yet again and converged in the Valley of the Titans.
verses.5:23: And David inquired through the Lord, and the Lord said, "You shall not go up to meet them; turn away from them, and you shall come upon them near the place of weeping.
verses.5:24: And it shall be, when you hear the sound of the closing in from the grove of weeping, then you shall go down against them; for then the Lord will go out before you to strike in the battle of the foreigners."
verses.5:25: And David did just as the Lord commanded him, and he struck the foreigners from Gibeon as far as the land of Gezer.
verses.6:1: And David again gathered every young man from Israel, about seventy thousand.
verses.6:2: And David arose and went, along with all the people who were with him from the rulers of Judah on the ascent, to bring up from there the ark of God, over which the name of the Lord of Hosts was called, who sits upon the cherubim upon it.
verses.6:3: And he placed the ark of the Lord upon a new cart and carried it to the house of Amminadab, who was on the hill; and Uzzah and his brothers, the sons of Amminadab, drove the cart with the ark,
verses.6:4: and his brothers walked before the ark.
verses.6:5: And David and the sons of Israel were playing before the Lord on finely tuned instruments, with might and with songs, and with lyres, and with harps, and with tambourines, and with cymbals, and with flutes.
verses.6:6: And they came to the threshing floor of Nodab; and Uzzah stretched out his hand to the ark of God to steady it, and he grasped it, because the calf drew him aside to take hold of it.
verses.6:7: And the Lord was angry with Uzzah, and God struck him there; and he died there beside the ark of the Lord before God.
verses.6:8: And David was disheartened because the Lord had broken out with a breach against Uzzah; and that place was called Breach of Uzzah to this day.
verses.6:9: And David feared the Lord on that day, saying, "How shall the ark of the Lord come to me?"
verses.6:10: And David was unwilling to turn aside the ark of the covenant of the Lord to himself into the City of David; so David turned it aside into the house of Abeddara the Gittite.
verses.6:11: And the ark of the Lord remained in the house of Abeddara the Gittite three months; and the Lord blessed all the house of Abeddara and all that was his.
verses.6:12: And it was reported to King David, saying, "The Lord has blessed the house of Abeddara and all that is his on account of the ark of God." So David went and brought up the ark of the Lord from the house of Abeddara to the City of David with gladness.
verses.6:13: And there were with them bearing the ark seven choirs, and as a sacrifice a calf and a lamb.
verses.6:14: And David was playing on finely tuned instruments before the Lord, and David was clothed in an extraordinary robe.
verses.6:15: And David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the Lord with shouting and with the sound of a trumpet.
verses.6:16: Now it came to pass, as the ark came to the City of David, that Michal the daughter of Saul looked down through the window and saw King David dancing and playing music before the Lord; and she despised him in her heart.
verses.6:17: And they brought the ark of the Lord and set it in its place in the midst of the tent which David had pitched for it; and he offered for it burnt offerings before the Lord, and peace offerings.
verses.6:18: And David finished offering up the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, and he blessed the people in the name of the Lord of Hosts.
verses.6:19: And he distributed to all the people, to all the host of Israel from Dan to Beersheba, from man to woman, to each a cake of bread, and a hearth-baked cake, and a wafer from the frying pan; and all the people departed, each one to his own house.
verses.6:20: And David returned to bless his own house; and Michal the daughter of Saul went out to meet David, and blessed him, and said, "How glorified today is the king of Israel, who uncovered himself today in the eyes of the maidservants of his servants, just as one of the dancers utterly uncovers himself!"
verses.6:21: And David said to Michal, "Before the Lord I will dance! Blessed be the Lord, who chose me above your father and above all his house, to appoint me as ruler over His people, over Israel; and I will play and dance before the Lord,
verses.6:22: and I will yet again uncover myself in this way, and I will be worthless in your eyes, and with the maidservants of whom you said that I was glorified."
verses.6:23: And Michal the daughter of Saul had no child until the day she died.
verses.7:1: And it came to pass, when the king sat in his house, and the Lord had given him an inheritance all around from all his surrounding enemies,
verses.7:2: that the king said to Nathan the prophet, "Behold now, I dwell in a house of cedar, yet the ark of God sits in the midst of the tent."
verses.7:3: And Nathan said to the king, "All that is in your heart, go and do, for the Lord is with you."
verses.7:4: And it came to pass in that night that the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,
verses.7:5: "Go and say to My servant David, 'Thus says the Lord: You shall not build Me a house for Me to dwell in.
verses.7:6: For I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought up the sons of Israel out of Egypt until this day, but I have been walking about in a lodging and in a tent.
verses.7:7: In all the places where I walked among all Israel, have I ever spoken to any one tribe of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd My people Israel, saying, "Why have you not built Me a house of cedar?"'
verses.7:8: And now, thus you shall say to My servant David, 'Thus says the Lord Almighty: I took you from the sheepfold, that you should be ruler over My people, over Israel,
verses.7:9: and I was with you wherever you went, and I utterly destroyed all your enemies from before your face, and I made you renowned, like the name of the great ones who are on the earth.
verses.7:10: And I will appoint a place for My people Israel and will plant them, and they shall dwell by themselves and shall be anxious no more; nor shall a son of iniquity afflict them anymore, as from the beginning,
verses.7:11: from the days that I appointed judges over My people Israel. And I will give you rest from all your enemies, and the Lord will declare to you that you shall build a house for Him.
verses.7:12: And it shall be, when your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, that I will raise up your seed after you, who shall come from your body, and I will prepare his kingdom.
verses.7:13: He shall build Me a house for My name, and I will establish his throne forever.
verses.7:14: I will be a Father to him, and he shall be a son to Me. And if his iniquity should come, I will reprove him with a rod of men and with the strokes of the sons of men.
verses.7:15: Yet My mercy I will not withdraw from him, just as I withdrew it from those whom I removed from before My face.
verses.7:16: And his house and his kingdom shall be made sure forever before Me, and his throne shall be established forever.'"
verses.7:17: According to all these words and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.
verses.7:18: Then King David went in and sat before the Lord, and he said, "Who am I, my Lord, O Lord, and what is my house, that You have loved me thus far?
verses.7:19: And I was made very small before You, my Lord, yet You have spoken concerning the house of Your servant for a great while to come; and this is the law of man, my Lord, O Lord.
verses.7:20: And what more shall David add to speak to You? And now You know Your servant, O Lord.
verses.7:21: Because of Your servant You have done it; and according to Your own heart You have done all this greatness, to make it known to Your servant, so as to magnify You,
verses.7:22: O Lord, my Lord; for there is none like You, nor is there any God besides You, in all that we have heard with our ears.
verses.7:23: And what other nation on the earth is like Your people Israel—how God led them to redeem for Himself a people, for You to establish a name, to work greatness and glorious manifestation, for You to drive out from before Your people, whom You redeemed for Yourself out of Egypt, nations and tents?
verses.7:24: And You have prepared for Yourself Your people Israel to be a people forever; and You, O Lord, have become their God.
verses.7:25: And now, my Lord, confirm forever the word which You have spoken concerning Your servant and his house, O Lord Almighty, God of Israel; and now, just as You have spoken,
verses.7:26: may Your name be magnified forever.
verses.7:27: O Lord Almighty, God of Israel, You have uncovered the ear of Your servant, saying, 'I will build a house for you.' Therefore Your servant has found it in his heart to pray this prayer to You.
verses.7:28: And now, my Lord, O Lord, You are God, and Your words shall be true, and You have spoken these good things concerning Your servant.
verses.7:29: And now begin and bless the house of Your servant, that it may be forever before You; for it is You, my Lord, O Lord, who have spoken, and from this blessing the house of Your servant shall be blessed forever."
verses.8:1: And it came to pass after this that David struck the Philistines and put them to flight; and David took the set-apart territory from the hand of the Philistines.
verses.8:2: And David struck Moab, and measured them with cords, making them lie down on the ground; and the two lines were to be put to death, and the two lines he kept alive. And Moab became servants to David, bringing tribute.
verses.8:3: And David struck Hadarezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to establish his hand upon the river Euphrates.
verses.8:4: And David captured from him one thousand chariots and seven thousand horsemen and twenty thousand footmen; and David disabled all the chariots, yet reserved for himself one hundred chariots.
verses.8:5: And Syria of Damascus came to help Hadarezer king of Zobah, and David struck among the Syrians twenty-two thousand men.
verses.8:6: Then David placed a garrison in Syria around Damascus, and the Syrians became servants to David, bringing tribute. And the Lord saved David wherever he went.
verses.8:7: And David took the golden bracelets which he had made for the servants of Hadarezer king of Zobah, and brought them to Jerusalem; and Shishak king of Egypt took them when he went up to Jerusalem in the days of Jeroboam the son of Solomon.
verses.8:8: And from Masbak, from the choice cities of Hadarezer, King David took exceedingly much bronze; with it Solomon made the bronze sea, and the pillars, and the lavers, and all the vessels.
verses.8:9: And Tou king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadarezer,
verses.8:10: so Tou sent Jedduran his son to King David, to inquire after his peace and to bless him because he had struck Hadarezer and struck him down, for he was opposed to Hadarezer; and in his hands were vessels of silver, vessels of gold, and vessels of bronze.
verses.8:11: These also the king consecrated to the Lord, together with the silver and the gold which he had consecrated from all the cities that he had subdued:
verses.8:12: from Idumea, and from the land of Moab, and from the sons of Ammon, and from the Philistines, and from Amalek, and from the spoil of Hadarezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
verses.8:13: And David made a name for himself; and as he returned, he struck Idumea in Gebelem, to the number of eighteen thousand.
verses.8:14: And he placed a garrison in Idumea, throughout all Idumea, and all the Idumeans became servants to the king. And the Lord saved David wherever he went.
verses.8:15: And David reigned over Israel; and he executed judgment and righteousness over all his people.
verses.8:16: And Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army, and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahijah was over the records,
verses.8:17: and Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were priests, and Asa was the scribe,
verses.8:18: and Benaiah the son of Janak was counselor, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David were chiefs of the court.
verses.9:1: And David said, "Is there still anyone left of the house of Saul, that I may show him mercy for the sake of Jonathan?"
verses.9:2: Now there was a servant of the house of Saul whose name was Ziba, and they called him to David. And the king said to him, "Are you Ziba?" And he said, "I am your servant."
verses.9:3: And the king said, "Is there still a man left of the house of Saul, that I may show him the mercy of God?" And Ziba said to the king, "There is still a son of Jonathan, stricken in his feet."
verses.9:4: And the king said, "Where is he?" And Ziba said to the king, "Behold, he is in the house of Machir the son of Amaer, from Lo Debar."
verses.9:5: Then King David sent and brought him from the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lo Debar.
verses.9:6: And Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to King David, and he fell on his face and paid homage to him. And David said to him, "Mephibosheth!" And he said, "Behold your servant."
verses.9:7: And David said to him, "Do not be afraid, for I will surely show mercy to you for the sake of Jonathan your father, and I will restore to you all the land of Saul your father's father; and you shall eat bread at my table continually."
verses.9:8: Then Mephibosheth paid homage and said, "Who am I, your servant, that you should look upon a dead dog such as I?"
verses.9:9: And the king called Ziba, the servant of Saul, and said to him, "All that belongs to Saul and to all his house I have given to your master's son.
verses.9:10: And you shall till the land for him, you and your sons and your servants, and you shall bring in bread for your master's son, and he shall eat bread; yet Mephibosheth, your master's son, shall eat bread continually at my table." Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
verses.9:11: Then Ziba said to the king, "According to all that my lord the king has commanded his servant, so your servant will do." And Mephibosheth ate at the table of David as one of the king's own sons.
verses.9:12: And Mephibosheth had a young son whose name was Micha. And all who dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants of Mephibosheth.
verses.9:13: So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem, for he ate continually at the king's table; and he was lame in both his feet.
verses.10:1: Now it came to pass after this that the king of the sons of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.
verses.10:2: And David said, "I will show mercy to Hanun the son of Nahash, in the same manner as his father showed mercy to me." So David sent by the hand of his servants to comfort him concerning his father. And the servants of David came into the land of the sons of Ammon.
verses.10:3: And the princes of the sons of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, "Is it because David honors your father in your sight that he has sent comforters to you? Rather, has David not sent his servants to you so that they may search the city, spy it out, and inspect it?"
verses.10:4: So Hanun took the servants of David, and shaved their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle as far as their hips, and sent them away.
verses.10:5: And they reported to David concerning the men, and he sent to meet them, for the men were greatly dishonored. And the king said, "Remain in Jericho until your beards have grown, and then you shall return."
verses.10:6: And the sons of Ammon saw that the people of David had been put to shame. So the sons of Ammon sent and hired Syria and Rehob, twenty thousand foot soldiers, and the king of Amalek, one thousand men, and Istob, twelve thousand men.
verses.10:7: And David heard of it, and he sent Joab and all the army, the mighty men.
verses.10:8: And the sons of Ammon came out and drew up in battle array at the entrance of the gate, while those of Syria of Zobah, and Rehob, and Istob, and Amalek were by themselves in the field.
verses.10:9: And Joab saw that the front of the battle was against him both before him and behind him. So he chose from all the young men of Israel, and they drew up in battle array against Syria.
verses.10:10: And the rest of the people he delivered into the hand of Abishai his brother, and they drew up in battle array against the sons of Ammon.
verses.10:11: And he said, "If Syria becomes too strong for me, then you shall be for my deliverance; and if the sons of Ammon become too strong for you, then we will come to deliver you.
verses.10:12: Be courageous, and let us be strong for our people and for the cities of our God; and the Lord will do what is good in His sight."
verses.10:13: So Joab and his people with him drew near to battle against Syria, and they fled from before him.
verses.10:14: And the sons of Ammon saw that Syria had fled, and they fled from before Abishai and entered into the city. Then Joab turned back from the sons of Ammon, and they came to Jerusalem.
verses.10:15: And Syria saw that they had been defeated before Israel, and they gathered themselves together.
verses.10:16: And Hadarezer sent and gathered Syria from beyond the river Chalamak, and they came to Helam; and Shobach, the commander of the army of Hadarezer, went before them.
verses.10:17: And it was reported to David, and he gathered all Israel, and crossed over the Jordan, and they came to Helam. And David drew up in battle array against Syria, and they fought with him.
verses.10:18: And Syria fled from before Israel; and David destroyed from Syria seven hundred chariots and forty thousand horsemen, and he struck down Shobach the commander of his army, and he died there.
verses.10:19: And all the kings who were servants of Hadarezer saw that they had been defeated before Israel, and they went over to Israel and served them. And Syria was afraid to deliver the sons of Ammon anymore.
verses.11:1: Now it came to pass at the return of the year, at the time when kings go forth, that David sent Joab and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the sons of Ammon and laid siege to Rabbah. But David remained in Jerusalem.
verses.11:2: And it came to pass toward evening that David arose from his bed and walked upon the roof of the king's house; and from the roof he saw a woman bathing, and the woman was exceedingly beautiful in appearance.
verses.11:3: So David sent and inquired about the woman, and one said, "Is this not Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliab, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?"
verses.11:4: Then David sent messengers and took her; and he went in to her and lay with her, and she was purifying herself from her uncleanness. And she returned to her house.
verses.11:5: And the woman conceived; so she sent and told David, and said, "I am with child."
verses.11:6: Then David sent to Joab, saying, "Send me Uriah the Hittite." And Joab sent Uriah to David.
verses.11:7: And Uriah arrived and came in to him; and David inquired concerning the welfare of Joab, and the welfare of the people, and the welfare of the war.
verses.11:8: And David said to Uriah, "Go down to your house and wash your feet." So Uriah went out from the king's house, and a portion from the king went out after him.
verses.11:9: But Uriah slept at the king's door with the servants of his lord, and did not go down to his house.
verses.11:10: And they reported to David, saying, "Uriah did not go down to his house." So David said to Uriah, "Do you not come from a journey? Why is it that you did not go down to your house?"
verses.11:11: And Uriah said to David, "The ark and Israel and Judah dwell in tents, and my lord Joab and the servants of my lord are encamped upon the face of the field. Shall I then go into my house to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? How? As your soul lives, I will not do this thing."
verses.11:12: Then David said to Uriah, "Remain here today also, and tomorrow I will send you away." So Uriah remained in Jerusalem on that day and the next.
verses.11:13: And David invited him, and he ate and drank before him; and he made him drunk. And in the evening he went out to lie upon his bed with the servants of his lord, and he did not go down to his house.
verses.11:14: And it came to pass in the morning that David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
verses.11:15: And he wrote in the letter, saying, "Set Uriah opposite the fiercest battle, and you shall turn back from behind him, and he shall be struck down and die."
verses.11:16: And it came to pass, as Joab was keeping watch over the city, that he placed Uriah in the place where he knew that men of valor were.
verses.11:17: And the men of the city came out and fought with Joab; and some of the people, of the servants of David, fell and died, and Uriah the Hittite also.
verses.11:18: Then Joab sent and reported to King David all the matters of the war, to speak them to the king.
verses.11:19: And he commanded the messenger, saying, "When you have finished speaking all the matters of the war to the king,
verses.11:20: then it shall be, if the wrath of the king rises and he says to you, 'Why is it that you drew near to the city to fight? Did you not know that they would shoot arrows from atop the wall?
verses.11:21: Who struck down Abimelech the son of Jeroboam the son of Ner? Did not a woman cast a piece of a millstone upon him from atop the wall, so that he died in Thamasi? Why did you draw near to the wall?' then you shall say, 'Your servant Uriah the Hittite has died also.'"
verses.11:22: So the messenger of Joab went to the king in Jerusalem; and he came and reported to David all that Joab had told him, all the matters of the war. And David was angry with Joab, and said to the messenger, "Why did you draw near to the city to fight? Did you not know that you would be struck from the wall? Who struck down Abimelech the son of Jeroboam? Did not a woman cast a piece of a millstone upon him from the wall, so that he died in Thamasi? Why did you draw near to the wall?"
verses.11:23: And the messenger said to David, "Because the men prevailed against us and came out against us into the field, and we pressed upon them as far as the entrance of the gate;
verses.11:24: and the archers shot at your servants from atop the wall, and some of the king's servants died; and your servant Uriah the Hittite has died also."
verses.11:25: Then David said to the messenger, "Thus you shall say to Joab: 'Do not let this matter be evil in your sight, for the sword devours now in this way and now in that. Strengthen your battle against the city and pull it down.' And strengthen him."
verses.11:26: And the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband had died, and she mourned for her husband.
verses.11:27: And when the mourning had passed, David sent and brought her into his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done appeared evil in the sight of the Lord.
verses.12:1: And the Lord sent Nathan the prophet to David; and he came to him and said to him, "There were two men in one city, one rich and one poor.
verses.12:2: And the rich man had exceedingly many flocks and herds;
verses.12:3: but the poor man had nothing except one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and preserved and nourished; and it grew up together with him and with his sons. It ate of his bread and drank from his cup, and slept in his bosom, and was to him as a daughter.
verses.12:4: And a traveler came to the rich man, and he was unwilling to take from his own flocks and from his own herds to prepare for the wayfaring stranger who had come to him; instead he took the poor man's ewe lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him."
verses.12:5: And David was greatly kindled with wrath against the man; and David said to Nathan, "As the Lord lives, surely the man who has done this is a son of death,
verses.12:6: and he shall restore the ewe lamb sevenfold, because he has done this thing and because he showed no pity."
verses.12:7: And Nathan said to David, "You are the man who has done this! For thus says the Lord God of Israel: 'I am He who anointed you king over Israel, and I am He who delivered you from the hand of Saul;
verses.12:8: and I gave you the house of your master and the wives of your master into your bosom, and I gave you the house of Israel and of Judah; and if this is a small thing, I will add to you according to these things.
verses.12:9: Because you have despised the word of the Lord to do what is evil in His eyes—you have struck down Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and have taken his wife to be your wife, and have slain him with the sword of the sons of Ammon—
verses.12:10: therefore now the sword shall not depart from your house forever, because you have shown contempt and have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.'
verses.12:11: Thus says the Lord: 'Behold, I am raising up evil against you out of your own house, and I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he shall lie with your wives in the sight of this sun.
verses.12:12: For you acted in secret, but I will do this thing before all Israel and in the full sight of this sun.'"
verses.12:13: And David said to Nathan, "I have sinned against the Lord." And Nathan said to David, "The Lord also has put away your sin; you shall not die.
verses.12:14: However, because by this deed you have greatly provoked the enemies of the Lord, the son also who has been born to you shall surely die."
verses.12:15: Then Nathan departed to his house. And the Lord struck the child that the wife of Uriah bore to David, and it became ill.
verses.12:16: And David sought God on behalf of the child; and David kept a fast, and went in and spent the night upon the ground.
verses.12:17: And the elders of the house stood over him to raise him up from the ground, but he was unwilling, nor did he eat bread with them.
verses.12:18: And it came to pass on the seventh day that the child died. And the servants of David were afraid to report to him that the child was dead, for they said, "Behold, while the child was still alive, we spoke to him, and he did not listen to our voice. How then shall we tell him that the child is dead? He will do harm."
verses.12:19: And David perceived that his servants were whispering, and David understood that the child was dead. And David said to his servants, "Is the child dead?" And they said, "He is dead."
verses.12:20: Then David arose from the ground, washed and anointed himself, and changed his garments; and he went into the house of God and worshiped Him. Then he went into his own house and asked for bread to eat; and they set bread before him, and he ate.
verses.12:21: And his servants said to him, "What is this thing that you have done? For the sake of the child while he was still alive, you fasted and wept and kept vigil; yet when the child died, you arose and ate bread and drank."
verses.12:22: And David said, "While the child was still alive, I fasted and wept; for I said, 'Who knows whether the Lord will have mercy on me, and the child shall live?'
verses.12:23: But now he is dead; why do I fast like this? Can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me."
verses.12:24: Then David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and went in to her and lay with her; and she conceived and bore a son, and called his name Solomon. And the Lord loved him,
verses.12:25: and He sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and he called his name Jedidiah, because of the Lord.
verses.12:26: Now Joab fought against Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, and captured the royal city.
verses.12:27: And Joab sent messengers to David and said, "I have fought against Rabbah and have captured the city of waters.
verses.12:28: Now therefore gather the rest of the people, and encamp against the city and capture it first, lest I capture the city first and my name be called upon it."
verses.12:29: So David gathered all the people and went to Rabbah, and fought against it and captured it.
verses.12:30: And he took the crown of Melchol their king from his head; its weight was a talent of gold with precious stone, and it was on David's head. And he brought out exceedingly much spoil from the city.
verses.12:31: And he brought out the people who were in it, and set them to the saw and to iron threshing sledges, and made them pass through the brickkiln; and thus he did to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
verses.13:1: Now it came to pass after this that Absalom the son of David had a sister who was exceedingly fair in appearance, whose name was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.
verses.13:2: And Amnon was so distressed that he became ill because of Tamar his sister, for she was a virgin; and it seemed overwhelming in Amnon's eyes to do anything to her.
verses.13:3: Now Amnon had a companion whose name was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David's brother; and Jonadab was a very shrewd man.
verses.13:4: And he said to him, "What ails you, O son of the king, that you are so weak morning by morning? Will you not tell me?" And Amnon said to him, "I love Tamar, the sister of my brother Absalom."
verses.13:5: Then Jonadab said to him, "Lie down on your bed and pretend to be ill; and your father will come in to see you, and you shall say to him, 'Please let Tamar my sister come and feed me, and prepare food before my eyes, so that I may see it and eat from her hands.'"
verses.13:6: So Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill; and the king came in to see him. And Amnon said to the king, "Please let Tamar my sister come to me, and let her make two cakes before my eyes, and I will eat from her hand."
verses.13:7: Then David sent to Tamar at the house, saying, "Please go to the house of your brother and prepare food for him."
verses.13:8: So Tamar went to the house of Amnon her brother, and he was lying down. And she took the dough and kneaded it, and shaped cakes before his eyes, and cooked the cakes.
verses.13:9: And she took the pan and poured them out before him, but he refused to eat. Then Amnon said, "Have every man go out from my presence." And they sent every man out from his presence.
verses.13:10: Then Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into the inner chamber, that I may eat from your hand." And Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought them to Amnon her brother in the bedchamber.
verses.13:11: And she brought them near to him to eat; and he seized her and said to her, "Come, lie with me, my sister."
verses.13:12: But she said to him, "No, my brother, do not humiliate me, for such a thing is not to be done in Israel; do not commit this folly.
verses.13:13: And as for me, where shall I carry my reproach? And you shall be as one of the fools in Israel. Now therefore, please speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you."
verses.13:14: However, Amnon would not listen to her voice; and he overpowered her and humiliated her, and lay with her.
verses.13:15: Then Amnon hated her with an exceedingly great hatred, for the hatred with which he hated her was greater—the latter wickedness was greater than the first—than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, "Arise and depart."
verses.13:16: And Tamar spoke to him concerning this great wickedness, "Greater than the other that you have done to me is to send me away!" Yet Amnon would not listen to her voice.
verses.13:17: Then he called his young servant who was in charge of the house and said to him, "Put this woman out from me, and bolt the door behind her."
verses.13:18: Now she had on a long-sleeved tunic, for thus the virgin daughters of the king clothed themselves in their outer garments. And his attendant brought her out and bolted the door behind her.
verses.13:19: Then Tamar took ashes and put ashes upon her head, and tore the long-sleeved tunic that was on her, and laid her hands upon her head, and went on her way crying aloud.
verses.13:20: And Absalom her brother said to her, "Has Amnon your brother been with you? Now therefore, my sister, keep silent, for he is your brother; do not set your heart to speak of this matter." So Tamar dwelt as a widow in the house of Absalom her brother.
verses.13:21: And King David heard all these things and was exceedingly angry; yet he did not grieve the spirit of Amnon his son, because he loved him, for he was his firstborn.
verses.13:22: And Absalom spoke to Amnon neither evil nor good; for Absalom hated Amnon because he had humiliated Tamar his sister.
verses.13:23: And it came to pass after two full years that Absalom had sheepshearers in Baal-hazor, which is near Ephraim; and Absalom invited all the king's sons.
verses.13:24: And Absalom came to the king and said, "Behold, now, your servant has sheepshearers; please let the king and his servants go with your servant."
verses.13:25: But the king said to Absalom, "No, my son, let us not all go, so that we may not be a burden to you." And he pressed him, yet he would not go, and he blessed him.
verses.13:26: Then Absalom said, "If not, please let Amnon my brother go with us." And the king said to him, "Why should he go with you?"
verses.13:27: But Absalom pressed him, so he sent Amnon and all the king's sons with him. And Absalom made a feast like the feast of the king.
verses.13:28: Now Absalom commanded his young servants, saying, "Watch when the heart of Amnon is merry with wine; and when I say to you, strike Amnon and put him to death. Do not fear, for is it not I who command you? Be courageous and be sons of valor."
verses.13:29: And the young servants of Absalom did to Amnon just as Absalom had commanded them. Then all the king's sons arose, and each man mounted his mule and fled.
verses.13:30: And it came to pass, while they were on the way, that the report came to David, saying, "Absalom has struck down all the king's sons, and not even one of them is left."
verses.13:31: Then the king arose and tore his garments and lay upon the ground; and all his servants who stood around him tore their garments.
verses.13:32: Then Jonadab the son of Shimeah, David's brother, answered and said, "Do not let my lord the king say that he has put to death all the young men, the king's sons, for Amnon alone is dead; for by the decree of Absalom this was set from the day that he humiliated Tamar his sister.
verses.13:33: Now therefore, do not let my lord the king take the matter to heart, saying, 'All the king's sons are dead'; for Amnon alone is dead."
verses.13:34: Meanwhile Absalom fled. And the young man who was the watchman lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, many people were coming along the road behind him from the side of the mountain on the descent. And the watchman came and reported to the king and said, "I have seen men from the road of Oronen, from the side of the mountain."
verses.13:35: Then Jonadab said to the king, "Behold, the king's sons have arrived; according to the word of your servant, so it has come to pass."
verses.13:36: And it came to pass, as soon as he had finished speaking, behold, the king's sons came, and they lifted up their voice and wept; and the king also and all his servants wept with a great weeping.
verses.13:37: But Absalom fled and went to Tholmailem the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur, into Machad. And King David mourned for his son all the days.
verses.13:38: So Absalom fled and went to Geshur, and was there three years.
verses.13:39: And King David ceased from going out to Absalom, for he was comforted concerning Amnon, because he was dead.
verses.14:1: And Joab the son of Zeruiah knew that the heart of the king was toward Absalom.
verses.14:2: And Joab sent to Tekoa, and brought from there a wise woman, and said to her, "Mourn now, and put on garments of mourning, and do not anoint yourself with oil; and you shall be like a woman mourning over one who has died for these many days;
verses.14:3: and you shall come to the king and speak to him according to this word." And Joab put the words in her mouth.
verses.14:4: And the Tekoite woman went in to the king, and fell on her face to the ground, and bowed down before him, and said, "Save, O king, save!"
verses.14:5: And the king said to her, "What is the matter with you?" And she said, "Truly, I am a widow woman, and my husband has died.
verses.14:6: Moreover, your maidservant had two sons, and the two of them fought together in the field, and there was no one to deliver between them; and the one struck the other, his brother, and put him to death.
verses.14:7: And behold, the whole family has risen up against your maidservant, and they said, 'Give up him who struck his brother, and we will put him to death for the life of his brother whom he slew, and we will cut off even your heir.' And they will quench my ember that remains, so as not to leave to my husband a remnant and a name upon the face of the earth."
verses.14:8: And the king said, "Go in good health to your house, and I will give command concerning you."
verses.14:9: And the Tekoite woman said to the king, "Upon me, my lord, O king, be the iniquity, and upon the house of my father; and let the king and his throne be guiltless."
verses.14:10: And the king said, "Who is the one speaking to you? You shall bring him to me, and he shall not touch him anymore."
verses.14:11: And she said, "Let the king now remember the Lord his God, though the avenger of blood be multiplied to destroy, and they shall by no means cut off my son." And he said, "As the Lord lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the ground."
verses.14:12: And she said, "Let your maidservant now speak a word to my lord the king." And he said, "Speak."
verses.14:13: And the woman said, "Why have you devised such a thing against the people of God? Or is this word from the mouth of the king as a trespass, in that the king does not bring back his banished one?
verses.14:14: For we shall surely die, and we are like water poured out to waste upon the earth, which shall not be gathered up again; and God will take a life, even while devising to banish from Himself one who is banished.
verses.14:15: And now, the reason I have come to speak this word to the king my lord is because the people will see me, and your people will say, 'Let her now speak to the king, if perhaps the king will do the word of his maidservant;'
verses.14:16: for the king will hear; let him deliver his maidservant out of the hand of the man who seeks to cut off me and my son from the inheritance of God."
verses.14:17: And the woman said, "May the word of my lord the king now be for sacrifices; for as an angel of God, so is my lord the king to hear the good and the evil. And the Lord your God shall be with you."
verses.14:18: And the king answered and said to the woman, "Do not hide from me now the matter that I ask you." And the woman said, "Let my lord the king now speak."
verses.14:19: And the king said, "Is not the hand of Joab with you in all this?" And the woman said to the king, "As your soul lives, my lord, O king, no one can turn to the right hand or to the left from all that my lord the king has spoken; for your servant Joab himself commanded me, and he himself put all these words in the mouth of your maidservant;
verses.14:20: in order to turn around the appearance of this matter which your servant Joab has done, this craftiness. Yet my lord is wise according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all things that are in the earth."
verses.14:21: And the king said to Joab, "Behold now, I have done for you according to this word of yours; bring back the young man Absalom."
verses.14:22: And Joab fell on his face to the ground and bowed down and blessed the king; and Joab said, "Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your eyes, my lord, O king, because my lord the king has done the word of his servant."
verses.14:23: And Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
verses.14:24: And the king said, "Let him return to his own house, and let him not see my face." So Absalom returned to his own house, and did not see the face of the king.
verses.14:25: And there was no man in all Israel so exceedingly praised as Absalom; from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.
verses.14:26: And when he sheared his head—for it came to pass from one year's beginning to another that he sheared it, because it was heavy upon him—when he sheared it, he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels according to the royal shekel.
verses.14:27: And to Absalom were born three sons and one daughter, whose name was Tamar; she was an exceedingly beautiful woman, and she became the wife of Rehoboam the son of Solomon, and bore to him Abiathar.
verses.14:28: And Absalom dwelt in Jerusalem two full years, and did not see the face of the king.
verses.14:29: And Absalom sent to Joab, to send him to the king, but he would not come to him; and he sent a second time to him, but he would not come.
verses.14:30: And Absalom said to his servants, "See, Joab's portion in the field is beside mine, and he has barley there; go and burn it with fire." And the servants of Absalom burned them, even the portion. And the servants of Joab came to him with their garments torn, and said, "The servants of Absalom have burned the portion with fire."
verses.14:31: And Joab arose and came to Absalom at the house, and said to him, "Why have your servants burned my portion with fire?"
verses.14:32: And Absalom said to Joab, "Behold, I sent to you, saying, 'Come here, and I will send you to the king to say, Why have I come from Geshur? It was good for me to be there.' And now, behold, I have not seen the face of the king; and if there is unrighteousness in me, then put me to death."
verses.14:33: And Joab went in to the king and told him, and he called for Absalom. And he went in to the king and bowed down before him, and fell on his face to the ground before the face of the king. And the king kissed Absalom.
verses.15:1: And it came to pass after these things that Absalom provided for himself chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him.
verses.15:2: And Absalom rose early and stood beside the way of the gate; and it was so, that whenever any man who had a lawsuit came to the king for judgment, Absalom called to him and said to him, "From what city are you?" And he said, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel."
verses.15:3: And Absalom said to him, "Behold, your words are good and clear, yet there is no one from the king to hear you."
verses.15:4: And Absalom said, "Who will appoint me judge in the land, so that every man who has a dispute and a cause may come to me, and I will give him justice?"
verses.15:5: And it came to pass, when a man drew near to bow down before him, that he stretched out his hand and took hold of him and kissed him.
verses.15:6: And Absalom did after this manner to all Israel who came to the king for judgment; and Absalom won for himself the heart of the men of Israel.
verses.15:7: And it came to pass at the end of forty years, that Absalom said to his father, "Let me go now and pay my vows which I have vowed to the Lord in Hebron;
verses.15:8: for your servant vowed a vow while I dwelt in Geshur in Syria, saying, 'If the Lord indeed brings me back to Jerusalem, then I will serve the Lord.'"
verses.15:9: And the king said to him, "Go in peace." And he arose and went to Hebron.
verses.15:10: And Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "When you hear the sound of the horn, then you shall say, 'King Absalom reigns in Hebron!'"
verses.15:11: And with Absalom went two hundred men out of Jerusalem who were invited; and they went in their simplicity, and did not know anything of the matter.
verses.15:12: And Absalom sent to Ahithophel the Tekonite, David's counselor, in his city Giloh, while he was offering sacrifices. And there came to be a mighty calamity, and the people kept growing numerous with Absalom.
verses.15:13: And a messenger came to David, saying, "The heart of the men of Israel has turned after Absalom."
verses.15:14: And David said to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem, "Arise, and let us flee, for there is no deliverance for us from the face of Absalom; make haste to depart, lest he make haste and overtake us, and thrust evil upon us and strike the city with the edge of the sword."
verses.15:15: And the servants of the king said to the king, "According to all that our lord the king chooses, behold, we are your servants."
verses.15:16: And the king went out, and all his house on foot; and the king left ten women of his concubines to keep the house.
verses.15:17: And the king went out, and all his servants on foot, and they stood at the Far House.
verses.15:18: And all his servants passed on beside him, and all the Hittites and all the Pelethites, and they stood by the olive tree in the wilderness; and all the people passed along beside him, and all those about him, and all the mighty men, and all the warriors, six hundred men, were present beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, the six hundred men who had come on foot to Gath, also marched before the face of the king.
verses.15:19: And the king said to Setthei the Gittite, "Why do you also go with us? Return and dwell with the king, for you are a stranger, and you have also migrated from your place.
verses.15:20: If you came only yesterday, shall I today make you wander with us? Indeed, you shall change your place of dwelling. Yesterday was your departure, and shall I today move you to go with us, seeing that I go wherever I may go? Return, and take back your brethren with you, and the Lord will deal with you in mercy and truth."
verses.15:21: And Ittai answered the king and said, "As the Lord lives, and as my lord the king lives, surely in whatever place my lord shall be, whether for death or for life, even there shall your servant be."
verses.15:22: And the king said to Setthei, "Come, and cross over with me." So Setthei the Gittite passed over, and all his servants, and all the multitude that was with him.
verses.15:23: And all the land wept with a loud voice; and all the people passed along in the brook of the cedars, and the king crossed over the brook Kidron; and all the people and the king passed along toward the way of the wilderness.
verses.15:24: And behold, Zadok also came, and all the Levites with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of the Lord from Baithar; and they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar went up until all the people had finished passing out of the city.
verses.15:25: And the king said to Zadok, "Carry back the ark of God into the city; if I find favor in the eyes of the Lord, He will also bring me back and show me both it and its beauty;
verses.15:26: and if He says thus, 'I have no delight in you,' behold, here I am; let Him do to me according to what is good in His eyes."
verses.15:27: And the king said to Zadok the priest, "See, you are returning to the city in peace, and Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan the son of Abiathar, your two sons, with you;
verses.15:28: see, I am encamped in Araboth of the wilderness until word comes from you to bring me report."
verses.15:29: And Zadok and Abiathar carried the ark back to Jerusalem, and they remained there.
verses.15:30: And David went up by the ascent of the olive trees with his head covered, and he went barefoot; and all the people who were with him covered each man his head, and they went up, going up and weeping.
verses.15:31: And it was told David, saying, "Ahithophel also is among those who are conspiring with Absalom." And David said, "Frustrate now the counsel of Ahithophel, O Lord my God."
verses.15:32: And David was coming as far as Roos, where he worshiped God there; and behold, Hushai the Archite, David's companion, came to meet him, having torn his tunic and with earth upon his head.
verses.15:33: And David said to him, "If you pass over with me, then you shall be a burden upon me;
verses.15:34: but if you return to the city and say to Absalom, 'Your brethren have passed over, and the king your father has passed over behind me; and now I am your servant, O king, let me live; I was the servant of your father formerly and until now, and now I am your servant,' then you shall frustrate for me the counsel of Ahithophel.
verses.15:35: And behold, Zadok and Abiathar the priests are there with you; and it shall be that whatever word you hear out of the king's house, you shall report it to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests.
verses.15:36: Behold, there with them are their two sons, Ahimaaz the son of Zadok and Jonathan the son of Abiathar; and by their hand you shall send to me every word that you hear."
verses.15:37: So Hushai, David's companion, went into the city, and Absalom was entering into Jerusalem.
verses.16:1: Now David had passed a little beyond Ros, and behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth came to meet him with a pair of saddled donkeys, and upon them were two hundred loaves of bread, one hundred clusters of raisins, one hundred dates, and a skin of wine.
verses.16:2: And the king said to Ziba, "What are these for?" And Ziba said, "The beasts of burden are for the household of the king to ride on, and the loaves of bread and the dates are for the young men to eat, and the wine is for those who grow faint in the wilderness to drink."
verses.16:3: And the king said, "And where is the son of your master?" And Ziba said to the king, "Behold, he remains in Jerusalem, for he said, 'Today the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my father.'"
verses.16:4: Then the king said to Ziba, "Behold, all that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours." And Ziba said, "I bow down; may I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king."
verses.16:5: Now King David came as far as Bahurim; and behold, from there a man came out from the kindred of the house of Saul, and his name was Shimei the son of Gera; he came forth, coming out and cursing,
verses.16:6: and throwing stones at David and at all the servants of King David; and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on the left hand of the king.
verses.16:7: And thus Shimei spoke while he cursed: "Get out, get out, you man of blood and lawless man!
verses.16:8: The Lord has brought back upon you all the blood of the house of Saul, because you reigned in his place, and the Lord has delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son; and behold, you are in your calamity, because you are a man of blood."
verses.16:9: Then Abishai the son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me cross over now and take off his head."
verses.16:10: And the king said, "What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? Let him alone, and so let him curse, because the Lord has told him to curse David; and who shall say, 'Why have you done thus?'"
verses.16:11: And David said to Abishai and to all his servants, "Behold, my own son who came forth from my body seeks my life; and how much more now this Benjamite! Let him alone to curse, for the Lord has spoken to him.
verses.16:12: Perhaps the Lord will look upon my affliction, and will return good to me in place of his cursing this day."
verses.16:13: So David and his men went along the road; and Shimei walked along the side of the mountain opposite him, going along and cursing, and throwing stones from beside him and flinging dust.
verses.16:14: And the king and all his people arrived weary, and they refreshed themselves there.
verses.16:15: Now Absalom and all the men of Israel entered into Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.
verses.16:16: And it came to pass, when Hushai the Archite, David's friend, came to Absalom, that Hushai said to Absalom, "Long live the king!"
verses.16:17: And Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this your kindness toward your friend? Why did you not depart with your friend?"
verses.16:18: And Hushai said to Absalom, "No, but following the one whom the Lord and this people and all the men of Israel have chosen, his I will be, and with him I will abide.
verses.16:19: And secondly, whom shall I serve? Should it not be before his son? Just as I served before your father, so shall I be before you."
verses.16:20: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Give counsel among yourselves as to what we should do."
verses.16:21: And Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Go in to your father's concubines, whom he left to keep the house; and all Israel will hear that you have disgraced your father, and the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened."
verses.16:22: So they pitched the tent for Absalom upon the housetop, and Absalom went in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.
verses.16:23: Now the counsel of Ahithophel, which he gave in those former days, was as when one would inquire at the word of God; so was all the counsel of Ahithophel, both to David and to Absalom.
verses.17:1: Moreover Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Let me now choose for myself twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David tonight.
verses.17:2: And I will come upon him while he is weary and weak of hands, and I will terrify him, and all the people who are with him will flee, and I will strike down the king alone;
verses.17:3: and I will bring back all the people to you, as a bride returns to her husband; you seek the life of only one man, and all the people shall be in peace."
verses.17:4: And the word was right in the eyes of Absalom and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.
verses.17:5: Then Absalom said, "Now call Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear what is in his mouth as well."
verses.17:6: So Hushai came in to Absalom; and Absalom spoke to him, saying, "Ahithophel has spoken after this manner. Shall we act according to his word? If not, you speak."
verses.17:7: And Hushai said to Absalom, "This counsel that Ahithophel has given is not good at this time."
verses.17:8: Hushai also said, "You know your father and his men, that they are exceedingly mighty, and they are bitter in their soul, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the field, and like a fierce wild sow in the plain; and your father is a man of war, and he will surely not let the people lodge.
verses.17:9: For behold, even now he is hidden in one of the hills, or in one of the other places; and it shall come to pass, when he falls upon them at the first, that whoever hears of it will hear and say, 'There has been a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom!'
verses.17:10: And even he who is a man of might, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will utterly melt away; for all Israel knows that your father is mighty, and those who are with him are men of might.
verses.17:11: Therefore I surely advise thus: let all Israel be completely gathered to you, from Dan even to Beersheba, like the sand that is by the sea for multitude, with your own presence going in the midst of them;
verses.17:12: and we shall come upon him in whichever of the places we may find him there, and we shall encamp upon him as the dew falls upon the earth; and of him and of the men who are with him we shall not leave even one.
verses.17:13: And if he withdraws into a city, then all Israel shall take ropes to that city, and we shall drag it down into the brook, so that not even a stone is left there."
verses.17:14: And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the good counsel of Ahithophel." For the Lord had commanded to frustrate the counsel of Ahithophel, so that the Lord might bring all the evil upon Absalom.
verses.17:15: Then Hushai the Archite said to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, "Thus and so Ahithophel counseled Absalom and the elders of Israel, and thus and so I have counseled.
verses.17:16: Now therefore send quickly and tell David, saying, 'Do not lodge tonight in Araboth of the wilderness, but by all means hasten to cross over, lest he prevail upon the king and all the people who are with him.'"
verses.17:17: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at the spring of Rogel, and a maidservant went and told them, and they were to go and report to King David, for they could not let themselves be seen entering the city.
verses.17:18: Yet a young man saw them, and they reported it to Absalom; so both of them departed quickly and entered into the house of a man in Bahurim, who had a cistern in his courtyard, and they went down there.
verses.17:19: And the woman took and spread a covering over the mouth of the cistern, and dried crushed grain upon it; and the matter was not known.
verses.17:20: Then the servants of Absalom came to the woman at the house and said, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" And the woman said to them, "They have passed a little beyond the water." And they searched and did not find them, and they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.17:21: Now it came to pass, after they had departed, that they came up out of the cistern, and went and told King David, and said to David, "Arise and cross over the water quickly, for thus Ahithophel has counseled against you."
verses.17:22: So David and all the people who were with him arose and crossed the Jordan; by the morning light, not even one was missing who had not crossed over the Jordan.
verses.17:23: Now when Ahithophel saw that his counsel had not been followed, he saddled his donkey, and arose and went to his house, to his own city; and he gave charge to his household, and hanged himself and died, and he was buried in the tomb of his father.
verses.17:24: Then David came to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.
