verses.17:25: And Absalom set Amasa over the army in place of Joab; now Amasa was the son of a man whose name was Jether the Israelite, who had gone in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, the brother of Zeruiah, the mother of Joab.
verses.17:26: And all Israel and Absalom encamped in the land of Gilead.
verses.17:27: And it came to pass, when David came to Mahanaim, that Uesbi the son of Nahash from Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim,
verses.17:28: brought ten beds, and rugs, and ten basins, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and barley meal, and beans, and lentils,
verses.17:29: and honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheeses of cattle; and they presented them to David and to the people who were with him to eat, for they said, "The people are hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness."
verses.18:1: And David inspected the people who were with him, and set over them captains of thousands and captains of hundreds.
verses.18:2: And David sent forth the people: a third under the hand of Joab, and a third under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, the brother of Joab, and a third under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And David said to the people, "Surely I also will go forth with you."
verses.18:3: And they said, "You shall not go forth; for if we flee away, they will not set their heart upon us; and if half of us die, they will not set their heart upon us, for you are as ten thousand of us. And now it is good that you be a help to us in the city to aid us."
verses.18:4: And the king said to them, "Whatever is pleasing in your eyes I will do." And the king stood by the side of the gate, and all the people marched out by hundreds and by thousands.
verses.18:5: And the king commanded Joab, and Abishai, and Ittai, saying, "Spare for my sake the young man Absalom." And all the people heard as the king gave charge to all the commanders concerning Absalom.
verses.18:6: And all the people went out into the forest against Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.
verses.18:7: And the people of Israel were defeated there before the servants of David, and the slaughter was great on that day, twenty thousand men.
verses.18:8: And the battle there was spread out over the face of all the land; and the forest devoured more of the people than those whom the sword devoured among the people on that day.
verses.18:9: And Absalom met the servants of David; and Absalom was riding upon his mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of the great oak, and his head was caught in the oak, and he was suspended between heaven and earth, while the mule beneath him passed on.
verses.18:10: And a certain man saw it, and reported to Joab, and said, "Behold, I have seen Absalom hanging in the oak."
verses.18:11: And Joab said to the man who reported it, "And behold, you saw him! Why did you not strike him to the ground? Then I would have given you ten pieces of silver and one belt."
verses.18:12: But the man said to Joab, "Even if I were weighing out a thousand shekels of silver upon my hands, I would by no means lay my hand upon the son of the king; for in our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, 'Guard for me the young man Absalom,
verses.18:13: so as not to do wrong against his life.' And no matter will be hidden from the king, and you yourself will stand in opposition."
verses.18:14: And Joab said, "I will begin this; I will not wait thus before you." And Joab took three darts in his hand, and they thrust them into the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the heart of the oak.
verses.18:15: And ten young men who bore Joab's armor surrounded him, and struck Absalom and put him to death.
verses.18:16: And Joab blew the horn, and the people turned back from pursuing after Israel, for Joab spared the people.
verses.18:17: And he took Absalom and cast him into a great chasm in the forest, into the great pit, and raised up over him a very great heap of stones. And all Israel fled, each man to his tent.
verses.18:18: Now Absalom, while he was still alive, had set up for himself the pillar in which he was taken, and had erected it to take for himself—the pillar that is in the Valley of the King—for he said he had no son to bring his name to remembrance; and he called the pillar the Hand of Absalom, to this day.
verses.18:19: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, "Let me run now and bring good tidings to the king, that the Lord has vindicated him from the hand of his enemies."
verses.18:20: And Joab said to him, "You are not a man of good tidings on this day, and you shall bear good tidings on another day; but on this day you shall not bear good tidings, because the son of the king is dead."
verses.18:21: Then Joab said to the Cushite, "Go, report to the king all that you have seen." And the Cushite bowed down to Joab and went out.
verses.18:22: And Ahimaaz the son of Zadok spoke yet again and said to Joab, "Let it be that I also run after the Cushite." And Joab said, "Why do you run for this, my son? Come, you have no good tidings to profit you in going."
verses.18:23: And he said, "For what if I run?" And Joab said to him, "Run." So Ahimaaz ran by the way of Kechar, and outran the Cushite.
verses.18:24: Now David was sitting between the two gates. And the watchman went up to the roof of the gate by the wall, and lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a man running alone before him.
verses.18:25: And the watchman cried out and reported to the king. And the king said, "If he is alone, there are good tidings in his mouth." And he came on steadily and drew near.
verses.18:26: And the watchman saw another man running, and the watchman called out at the gate and said, "Behold, another man running alone!" And the king said, "He also brings good tidings."
verses.18:27: And the watchman said, "I see the running of the first like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok." And the king said, "He is a good man, and indeed he will come with good tidings."
verses.18:28: And Ahimaaz called out and said to the king, "Peace!" And he bowed down to the king with his face to the earth, and said, "Blessed be the Lord your God, who has delivered up the men who hated their hand against my lord the king."
verses.18:29: And the king said, "Is it peace with the young man Absalom?" And Ahimaaz said, "I saw the great multitude at the sending of the king's servant Joab and your servant, and I did not know what was there."
verses.18:30: And the king said, "Turn aside, stand fast here." And he turned aside and stood.
verses.18:31: And behold, the Cushite arrived and said to the king, "Let my lord the king receive good tidings, for the Lord has vindicated you today from the hand of all who rose up against you."
verses.18:32: And the king said to the Cushite, "Is it peace with the young man Absalom?" And the Cushite said, "May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who have risen up against him for evil, become like the young man."
verses.19:1: And the king was deeply troubled, and went up to the upper chamber of the gate and wept. And thus he spoke as he went: "My son, my son Absalom! Who would grant my death instead of you? I instead of you, Absalom, my son, my son!"
verses.19:2: And it was reported to Joab, saying, "Behold, the king is weeping and mourning over Absalom."
verses.19:3: And the deliverance on that day became mourning for all the people, because the people heard on that day, saying, "The king is grieved over his son."
verses.19:4: And the people stole away on that day to enter into the city, just as people who are ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.
verses.19:5: And the king hid his face; and the king cried out with a loud voice, saying, "My son Absalom, Absalom my son!"
verses.19:6: And Joab came to the king into the house and said, "You have put to shame today the countenance of all your servants who delivered you today, and the life of your sons and of your daughters, and the life of your wives and of your concubines,
verses.19:7: in loving those who hate you and hating those who love you; and you have declared today that your commanders and servants are nothing. For I know today that if Absalom were alive and all of us today were dead, then it would have been right in your eyes.
verses.19:8: Now therefore arise, go out, and speak to the heart of your servants; for I have sworn by the Lord that if you do not go out today, not a single man shall lodge with you this night. And recognize for yourself that this will be worse for you than all the evil that has come upon you from your youth until now."
verses.19:9: Then the king arose and sat in the gate. And all the people reported, saying, "Behold, the king is sitting in the gate." So all the people came before the king. Now Israel had fled, every man to his tents.
verses.19:10: And all the people were disputing among all the tribes of Israel, saying, "King David rescued us from the hand of all our enemies, and he himself delivered us from the hand of the foreigners; and now he has fled from the land and from his kingdom and from Absalom,
verses.19:11: whom we anointed over us—he has died in battle. Now therefore, why are you silent about returning to the king?" And the word of all Israel came to the king.
verses.19:12: And King David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, "Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, 'Why are you the last to return to the king to his house? And the word of all Israel has come to the king.
verses.19:13: You are my brethren, you are my bones and my flesh; why then are you the last to bring back the king to his house?'
verses.19:14: And to Amasa you shall say, 'Are you not my bone and my flesh? Now may God do so to me, and more also, if you shall not be commander of the army before me all the days in place of Joab.'"
verses.19:15: And he inclined the heart of every man of Judah, even to a single man; and they sent to the king, saying, "Return, you and all your servants."
verses.19:16: So the king returned and came to the Jordan. And the men of Judah came to Gilgal to go to meet the king, to bring the king across the Jordan.
verses.19:17: And Shimei the son of Gera, the son of the Jeminite, from Bahurim, hastened and came down with the men of Judah to meet King David,
verses.19:18: and a thousand men of Benjamin were with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons with him and his twenty servants with him; and they made straight across the Jordan before the king,
verses.19:19: and they performed the service of bringing the king across; and the ferry crossed over to rouse the household of the king and to do what was right in his eyes. And Shimei the son of Gera fell on his face before the king as he was crossing the Jordan,
verses.19:20: and said to the king, "Do not let my lord reckon iniquity, and do not remember all the wrong that your servant committed on the day when my lord went out from Jerusalem, that the king should take it to his heart;
verses.19:21: for your servant knows that I have sinned, and behold, I have come today first of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king."
verses.19:22: And Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered and said, "Shall Shimei not be put to death for this, because he cursed the anointed of the Lord?"
verses.19:23: And David said, "What have I to do with you, sons of Zeruiah, that you should become an adversary to me today? Today not a single man of Israel shall be put to death; for do I not know that today I reign as king over Israel?"
verses.19:24: And the king said to Shimei, "You shall surely not die." And the king swore to him.
verses.19:25: And Mephibosheth the son of the son of Saul came down to meet the king; and he had not tended his feet, nor pared his nails, nor trimmed his mustache, and had not washed his garments from the day the king departed until the day he arrived in peace.
verses.19:26: And it came to pass, when he came into Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said to him, "Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?"
verses.19:27: And Mephibosheth said to him, "My lord the king, my servant deceived me; for your servant said to him, 'Saddle the donkey for me, that I may mount it and go with the king,' because your servant is lame.
verses.19:28: And he dealt craftily against your servant before my lord the king; yet my lord the king has done what is good openly, like an angel of God. Therefore do what is good in your eyes.
verses.19:29: For all the house of my father were nothing but men worthy of death to my lord the king, yet you set your servant among those who eat at your table. What just claim, therefore, do I still have, even to cry out any further to the king?"
verses.19:30: And the king said to him, "Why do you still speak your words? I have said, 'You and Ziba shall divide the field.'"
verses.19:31: And Mephibosheth said to the king, "Indeed, let him take it all, now that my lord the king has come in peace to his own house."
verses.19:32: And Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim and crossed the Jordan with the king, to escort him over the Jordan.
verses.19:33: Now Barzillai was an exceedingly aged man, eighty years old; and he had sustained the king while he dwelt in Mahanaim, for he was a very great man.
verses.19:34: And the king said to Barzillai, "Cross over with me, and I will sustain your old age with me in Jerusalem."
verses.19:35: And Barzillai said to the king, "How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?
verses.19:36: I am eighty years old today. Can I truly discern between good and bad, even to what is evil? Can your servant still taste what I eat or what I drink? Or can I still hear the voice of singing men and singing women? Why then should your servant still be a burden upon my lord the king?
verses.19:37: Your servant will go just a little way across the Jordan with the king; and why should the king repay me with such a reward?
verses.19:38: Let your servant remain, I pray, and I shall die in my own city beside the grave of my father and my mother. But behold, your servant Chimham will cross over with my lord the king; and do for him what is good in your eyes."
verses.19:39: And the king said, "Let Chimham cross over with me, and I will do for him what is good in your eyes; and all that you choose of me, I will do for you."
verses.19:40: And all the people crossed over the Jordan, and the king crossed over. And the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his own place.
verses.19:41: And the king crossed over to Gilgal, and Chimham crossed over with him; and all the people of Judah were crossing over with the king, and also half the people of Israel.
verses.19:42: And behold, all the men of Israel came to the king and said to the king, "Why have our brethren, the men of Judah, stolen you away, and brought the king and his household across the Jordan, and all the men of David with him?"
verses.19:43: And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel and said, "Because the king is near of kin to me. Why then are you so angry over this matter? Have we eaten anything at all from the king, or has he given a gift, or bestowed a portion upon us?"
verses.19:44: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah and said, "I have ten shares in the king, and I am the firstborn rather than you, and indeed I have more in David than you. Why then have you insulted me in this, and why was my word not counted first for me before Judah, to bring back my king?" Yet the words of the men of Judah were harsher than the words of the men of Israel.
verses.20:1: And there was one called there, a lawless man, and his name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Jeminite; and he blew the horn and said, "We have no portion in David, nor have we any inheritance in the son of Jesse! Every man to your tents, O Israel!"
verses.20:2: So all Israel went up from following David, to follow Sheba the son of Bichri; but the men of Judah clung to their king, from the Jordan even to Jerusalem.
verses.20:3: And David came to his house in Jerusalem. And the king took the ten women, his concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in a house of custody, and sustained them, and did not go in to them. So they were shut up until the day of their death, living as widows.
verses.20:4: And the king said to Amasa, "Summon the men of Judah for me within three days, and you yourself stand here."
verses.20:5: So Amasa went to summon Judah, and he delayed beyond the appointed time which he had set for him.
verses.20:6: And David said to Abishai, "Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us greater harm than Absalom; now therefore, take with you the servants of your lord and pursue after him, lest he find for himself fortified cities and cast a shadow over our eyes."
verses.20:7: So Abishai and the men of Joab went out after him, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites and all the mighty men; and they went out from Jerusalem to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.
verses.20:8: And when they were beside the great stone that is in Gibeon, Amasa came before them. Now Joab was girded with a cloak, his garment, and over it he was girded with a sword fastened upon his loins in its sheath; and the sword came out—it came out and fell.
verses.20:9: And Joab said to Amasa, "Are you in health, brother?" And the right hand of Joab took hold of the beard of Amasa to kiss him.
verses.20:10: And Amasa did not watch out for the sword that was in the hand of Joab; and Joab struck him with it in the abdomen, and his entrails poured out upon the ground, and he did not strike him a second time, and he died. Then Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.
verses.20:11: And a man of the young men of Joab stood over him and said, "Who favors Joab, and who is for David? Follow after Joab!"
verses.20:12: Now Amasa was wallowing in blood in the middle of the road. And when the man saw that all the people stood still, they moved Amasa from the road into a field, and he cast a garment over him, because he saw that everyone who came up to him stood still.
verses.20:13: And as soon as he was removed from the road, all the men of Israel passed on after Joab to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.
verses.20:14: And he passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel and to Beth Maacah; and all who were in Charri were gathered together, and he came after him.
verses.20:15: And they came and besieged him in Abel of Beth Maacah, and they poured out a siege mound against the city, and it stood against the outer rampart; and all the people who were with Joab were devising to throw down the wall.
verses.20:16: And a wise woman cried out from the wall and said, "Hear, hear! Say, I pray, to Joab, 'Draw near to this place,' and I will speak with him."
verses.20:17: And he drew near to her, and the woman said, "Are you Joab?" And he said, "I am." Then she said to him, "Hear the words of your maidservant." And Joab said, "I am listening."
verses.20:18: And she spoke, saying, "They spoke a word in former times, saying, 'Inquiry was surely made in Abel and in Dan whether the things which the faithful of Israel established had failed; indeed, they shall surely inquire of one in Abel, and thus, whether they have failed.'
verses.20:19: I am of the peaceful strongholds of Israel, yet you seek to put to death a city and a mother city in Israel. Why do you swallow up the inheritance of the Lord?"
verses.20:20: And Joab answered and said, "Far be it from me, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or that I should destroy!
verses.20:21: This is not the matter. Rather, a man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, has lifted up his hand against King David. Give him to me alone, and I will depart from the city." And the woman said to Joab, "Behold, his head shall be thrown to you over the wall."
verses.20:22: Then the woman went to all the people, and she spoke to the whole city in her wisdom. And she cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and took it and threw it to Joab. Then he blew the horn, and they were dispersed from the city away from him, every man to his tents. And Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.
verses.20:23: Now Joab was over all the army of Israel, and Benaiah the son of Ahilud was over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites;
verses.20:24: and Adoniram was over the tribute, and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder,
verses.20:25: and Joshua was the scribe, and Zadok and Abiathar were priests,
verses.20:26: and Ira the Jairite was also a priest to David.
verses.21:1: Now there was a famine in the days of David for three years, year following year; and David sought the face of the Lord. And the Lord said, "Upon Saul and upon his house is iniquity because of his bloody slaughter, for he put the Gibeonites to death."
verses.21:2: And King David called the Gibeonites and spoke to them. Now the Gibeonites are not of the children of Israel, but rather of the blood of the Amorites, and the children of Israel had sworn to them; yet Saul sought to strike them down in his zeal for the children of Israel and Judah.
verses.21:3: And David said to the Gibeonites, "What shall I do for you, and with what shall I make atonement, so that you will bless the inheritance of the Lord?"
verses.21:4: And the Gibeonites said to him, "We have no silver and gold with Saul and with his house, nor do we have any man to put to death in Israel." And he said, "What do you say, that I may do it for you?"
verses.21:5: And they said to the king, "The man brought destruction upon us and pursued us, who schemed to destroy us utterly; let us blot him out, that he may not stand in any territory of Israel.
verses.21:6: Let seven men from his sons be given to us, and we will expose them to the sun for the Lord in Gibeon of Saul, chosen ones of the Lord." And the king said, "I will give them."
verses.21:7: But the king spared Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the oath of the Lord that was between them, even between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.
verses.21:8: So the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bore to Saul—Armoni and Mephibosheth—and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she bore to Serei the son of Barzillai the Meholathite,
verses.21:9: and he delivered them into the hand of the Gibeonites; and they exposed them to the sun on the mountain before the Lord, and those seven fell together. And they were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, at the beginning of the barley harvest.
verses.21:10: And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and pitched it for herself against the rock at the beginning of the barley harvest until water dropped upon them from heaven; and she did not allow the birds of heaven to rest upon them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
verses.21:11: And it was reported to David all that Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done. And they grew faint, and Dan the son of Joa, of the descendants of the giants, overtook them.
verses.21:12: And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men, the sons of Jabesh Gilead, who had stolen them from the open square of Baith, for the Philistines had set them up there in the day when the Philistines struck down Saul in Gilboa.
verses.21:13: And he brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son, and he gathered the bones of those who had been exposed to the sun.
verses.21:14: And they buried the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son, and of those who had been exposed to the sun, in the land of Benjamin, at the side, in the tomb of Kish his father; and they did all that the king had commanded. And God heeded the land after these things.
verses.21:15: Now there was again war between the Philistines and Israel; and David went down, and his servants with him, and they fought against the Philistines; and David went on.
verses.21:16: And Jesbi, who was among the offspring of Rapha—and the weight of his spear was three hundred shekels in weight of bronze, and he was girded with a club—intended to strike down David.
verses.21:17: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah came to his aid, and struck the Philistine and put him to death. Then the men of David swore, saying, "You shall no longer go out with us to battle, and you shall by no means quench the lamp of Israel."
verses.21:18: And it came to pass after these things that there was again war in Gath with the Philistines. Then Oebocha the Hastatothite struck down Seph, who was among the offspring of Rapha.
verses.21:19: And there was war in Rom with the Philistines; and Elhanan the son of Ariorgim the Bethlehemite struck down Godoliah the Hittite, and the shaft of his spear was like a weavers' beam.
verses.21:20: And there was again war in Gath; and there was a man of Madon, and the fingers of his hands and the toes of his feet were six and six, twenty-four in number; and he also was born to Rapha.
verses.21:21: And he reproached Israel, and Jonathan the son of Shimei, the brother of David, struck him down.
verses.21:22: These four were born as descendants of the giants in Gath, the house of Rapha, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.
verses.22:1: And David spoke the words of this song to the Lord on the day the Lord rescued him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
verses.22:2: And he said, A song: "O Lord, my rock and my stronghold, and He who delivers me for myself;
verses.22:3: my God shall be my guardian, I will trust in Him; my shield and the horn of my salvation, my upholder and my refuge of my salvation; from an unjust man You shall save me.
verses.22:4: I will call upon the Lord, who is worthy of praise, and from my enemies I shall be saved.
verses.22:5: For the crushings of death surrounded me; torrents of lawlessness terrified me.
verses.22:6: The pangs of death encircled me; the severities of death overtook me.
verses.22:7: When I am afflicted I will call upon the Lord, and to my God I will cry aloud; and He shall hear my voice from His temple, and my cry shall be in His ears.
verses.22:8: And the earth was troubled and shaken, and the foundations of heaven were thrown into turmoil and convulsed, because the Lord was angry with them.
verses.22:9: Smoke rose up in His wrath, and fire from His mouth shall devour; coals were kindled from Him.
verses.22:10: And He bowed the heavens and descended, and thick darkness was beneath His feet.
verses.22:11: And He sat upon cherubim and flew, and He was seen upon the wings of the wind.
verses.22:12: And He placed the darkness of His hiding place all around Him; His tent was darkness of waters; it thickened in the clouds of the air.
verses.22:13: From the radiance before Him coals of fire were kindled.
verses.22:14: The Lord thundered out of heaven, and the Most High gave forth His voice.
verses.22:15: And He sent forth arrows and scattered them, lightning, and threw them into dismay.
verses.22:16: And the channels of the sea appeared, and the foundations of the inhabited world were uncovered, at the rebuke of the Lord, from the blast of the breath of His wrath.
verses.22:17: He sent from on high and took me; He drew me out of many waters.
verses.22:18: He rescued me from my enemies of might, from those who hated me, because they had grown stronger than I.
verses.22:19: The days of my affliction overtook me, and the Lord became my support;
verses.22:20: and He led me forth into a broad place, and He delivered me, because He was well pleased with me.
verses.22:21: And the Lord recompensed me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands He recompensed me.
verses.22:22: For I kept the ways of the Lord, and I did not act impiously away from my God.
verses.22:23: For all His judgments were before me, and His ordinances—I did not depart from them.
verses.22:24: And I shall be blameless before Him, and I shall keep watch against my iniquity.
verses.22:25: And the Lord shall repay me according to my righteousness and according to the cleanness of my hands before His eyes.
verses.22:26: With the devout You will show Yourself devout, and with a perfect man You will show Yourself perfect;
verses.22:27: and with the chosen You will be chosen, and with the crooked You will show Yourself crooked.
verses.22:28: And the poor people You will save, and eyes upon the haughty You will bring low.
verses.22:29: For You are my lamp, O Lord, and the Lord shall brighten my darkness for me.
verses.22:30: For by You I shall run girded for action, and by my God I shall scale a wall.
verses.22:31: As for the Mighty One, His way is blameless; the word of the Lord is strong, refined by fire; He is a shield to all who trust in Him.
verses.22:32: Who is mighty besides the Lord? And who shall be a Creator besides our God?
verses.22:33: It is the Mighty One who strengthens me with power, and He shook out my way blameless;
verses.22:34: making my feet like those of deer, and setting me upon the high places;
verses.22:35: teaching my hands for war, and breaking a bow of bronze by my arm.
verses.22:36: And You gave me the defense of my salvation, and Your attentiveness multiplied me, into a broad space for my steps beneath me,
verses.22:37: and my legs were not shaken.
verses.22:38: I will pursue my enemies and wipe them out, and I will not turn back until I make an end of them;
verses.22:39: and I will crush them, and they shall not rise, and they shall fall beneath my feet.
verses.22:40: And You shall strengthen me with power for war; You shall bend down beneath me those who rise up against me.
verses.22:41: And You gave me the back of my enemies, those who hated me, and You put them to death.
verses.22:42: They shall cry out, and there is no helper—even to the Lord, and He did not heed them.
verses.22:43: And I ground them fine like the dust of the earth; like the mire of the thoroughfares I beat them thin.
verses.22:44: And You shall rescue me from the strife of peoples; You shall preserve me as the head of nations. A people whom I did not know served me;
verses.22:45: foreign sons dealt falsely with me; at the hearing of the ear they obeyed me;
verses.22:46: foreign sons shall be cast away, and they shall stumble out of their enclosures.
verses.22:47: The Lord lives! And blessed be my guardian, and my God shall be exalted, the guardian of my salvation!
verses.22:48: Mighty is the Lord, who gives vengeance to me, chastening peoples beneath me,
verses.22:49: and leading me out from my enemies; and from those who rise up against me You shall lift me on high; from a man of wrongdoings You shall rescue me.
verses.22:50: Therefore I will give thanks to You, O Lord, among the nations, and in Your name I will sing praises,
verses.22:51: magnifying the deliverances of His king, and showing mercy to His anointed, to David and to his seed forever." And these are the last words of David.
verses.23:1: Faithful is David the son of Jesse, and faithful is the man whom the Lord raised up over the anointed of the God of Jacob, and lovely are the psalms of Israel.
verses.23:2: The Spirit of the Lord spoke in me, and His word was upon my tongue.
verses.23:3: The God of Israel says; to me the Guardian out of Israel spoke, "Speak a parable: 'In man, how shall you strengthen the fear of the anointed?'"
verses.23:4: And in God, the light of morning, may the sun arise; in the morning the Lord did not pass by from brightness, and as from the rain of fresh grass out of the earth.
verses.23:5: For is not this my house with the Mighty One? For He has made with me an everlasting covenant, prepared at every season and kept, for this is all my salvation and every desire; for the lawless one shall by no means spring up.
verses.23:6: Like a thorn cast away are all of these, because they shall not be taken by the hand;
verses.23:7: and a man shall not toil among them; rather, with fullness of iron and the shaft of a spear, even with burning in fire, they shall be put to their shame.
verses.23:8: These are the names of the mighty men of David: Jebosthe the Canaanite is chief of the third; Adinon the Asonite, he drew his sword against eight hundred soldiers at one time.
verses.23:9: And after him was Eleanan the son of his father's brother, the son of Susei, who was among the three mighty men with David; and when he defied the Philistines, they were gathered together there for battle, and the men of Israel cried out.
verses.23:10: He arose and struck among the Philistines until his hand grew weary, and his hand clung to the sword; and the Lord worked a great deliverance in that day, and the people sat behind him only to strip them.
verses.23:11: And after him was Samaia the son of Asa the Aruchite; and the Philistines were gathered together at Theria, and there was a plot of the field full of lentils, and the people fled from before the Philistines.
verses.23:12: But he stood firm in the midst of the plot, and delivered it and struck down the Philistines; and the Lord worked a great deliverance.
verses.23:13: And three of the thirty went down, and they went down to Kadon to David, to the cave of Adullam; and a company of the Philistines was there, and they encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.23:14: And David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then in Bethlehem.
verses.23:15: And David longed and said, "Who will give me water to drink from the cistern in Bethlehem, which is in the gate?" Now the band of the Philistines was then in Bethlehem.
verses.23:16: And the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Philistines and drew water from the cistern in Bethlehem, which is in the gate, and took it and came to David; yet he would not drink it, and poured it out to the Lord.
verses.23:17: And he said, "Far be it from me, O Lord, to do this! Shall I drink the blood of the men who went at the peril of their lives?" And he would not drink it. These things the three mighty men did.
verses.23:18: And Abishai the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, he was chief among the three; and he lifted up his spear against three hundred slain men, and he had a name among the three.
verses.23:19: Of those three he was renowned, and he became a commander over them; yet he did not attain to the three.
verses.23:20: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, a man abounding in deeds from Kabzeel, he struck down the two sons of Ariel of Moab; and he also went down and struck down the lion in the midst of the pit on the day of snow.
verses.23:21: He also struck down the Egyptian man, a notable man; and in the hand of the Egyptian was a spear like the beam of a bridge; and he went down to him with a spear, and snatched the spear out of the Egyptian's hand, and slew him with his own spear.
verses.23:22: These things Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did, and he had a name among the three mighty men.
verses.23:23: Of the three he was renowned, yet he did not attain to the three; and David appointed him to his hearing. And these are the names of the mighty men of King David:
verses.23:24: Asahel the brother of Joab, he was among the thirty; Elhanan the son of Dodei his father's brother, in Bethlehem;
verses.23:26: Selles the Kelothite; Ira the son of Iska the Tekoite;
verses.23:27: Abiezer the Anothite, of the sons of the Anothite;
verses.23:28: Ellon the Ahohite; Noere the Netophathite.

verses.24:1: And the Lord again caused wrath to burn against Israel, and He stirred up David against them, saying, "Go, number Israel and Judah."
verses.24:2: And the king said to Joab the commander of the force who was with him, "Go now through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beersheba, and count the people, and I shall know the number of the people."
verses.24:3: And Joab said to the king, "May the Lord God add to the people as many as they are, and as many as they are a hundredfold, and may the eyes of my lord the king see it; yet why does my lord the king desire this thing?"
verses.24:4: Nevertheless, the word of the king prevailed against Joab and against the commanders of the host; and Joab and the commanders of the force went out from before the king to count the people of Israel.
verses.24:5: And they crossed over the Jordan and encamped in Aroel, on the right side of the city that is in the midst of the valley of Gad, and Eliezer.
verses.24:6: And they came to Gilead and to Thabason, which is Nadasai, and they arrived at Dan Eidan and Oudan, and went around to Sidon;
verses.24:7: and they came to Mapsar of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivite and of the Canaanite; and they came toward the south of Judah, to Beersheba,
verses.24:8: and they went about through all the land; and at the end of nine months and twenty days they came to Jerusalem.
verses.24:9: And Joab gave the number of the registration of the people to the king; and Israel was eight hundred thousand men of might who drew the sword, and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand fighting men.
verses.24:10: And David's heart struck him after he had numbered the people; and David said to the Lord, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done; now, O Lord, take away, I pray, the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."
verses.24:11: And David arose in the morning; and the word of the Lord came to Gad the prophet, David's seer, saying,
verses.24:12: "Go and speak to David, saying, 'Thus says the Lord: Three things I am laying upon you; choose for yourself one of them, and I will do it to you.'"
verses.24:13: And Gad came to David, and told him and said to him, "Choose for yourself what shall come to pass: whether three years of famine shall come upon you in your land, or three months for you to flee before your enemies while they pursue you, or that there be three days of pestilence in your land. Now therefore know and see what word I shall answer to Him who sent me."
verses.24:14: And David said to Gad, "I am in great distress on every side; I will fall now into the hand of the Lord, for His mercies are exceedingly many, but into the hands of man I will by no means fall."
verses.24:15: And David chose for himself the pestilence; and it was the days of the wheat harvest, and the Lord sent pestilence upon Israel from the morning until the hour of the midday meal; and the plague began among the people, and there died of the people from Dan even to Beersheba seventy thousand men.
verses.24:16: And the angel of God stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, and the Lord relented concerning the calamity and said to the angel who was destroying among the people, "It is enough now; stay your hand." And the angel of the Lord was by the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite.
verses.24:17: And David spoke to the Lord when he saw the angel striking among the people, and he said, "Behold, it is I who have done wrong; yet these, the sheep, what have they done? Let Your hand, I pray, be against me and against the house of my father."
verses.24:18: And Gad came to David on that day and said to him, "Go up and set up an altar to the Lord on the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite."
verses.24:19: And David went up according to the word of Gad, just as the Lord had commanded him.
verses.24:20: And Orna looked out and saw the king and his servants passing by above him; and Orna went out and bowed down to the king with his face to the ground.
verses.24:21: And Orna said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" And David said, "To purchase the threshing floor from you, in order to build an altar to the Lord." And the plague was restrained from upon the people.
verses.24:22: And Orna said to David, "Let my lord the king take and offer up to the Lord what is good in his eyes; behold, the oxen for a burnt offering, and the wheels and the gear of the oxen for wood."
verses.24:23: All these things Orna gave to the king; and Orna said to the king, "May the Lord your God bless you."
verses.24:24: And the king said to Orna, "No, for I will surely purchase it from you for a price, and I will not offer up to my Lord, my God, a burnt offering without cost." So David purchased the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
verses.24:25: And David built an altar there to the Lord, and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings; and Solomon added to the altar afterward, because it was small at the first. And the Lord heeded the land, and the plague was restrained from upon Israel.

notes.1:9: The Greek reads "a dreadful darkness" (skotos deinon), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to anguish or convulsion.
notes.1:12: The Greek reads "the people of Judah" (where the Hebrew has "the people of the LORD") and places "fasted" before "wept."
notes.1:18: The Greek does not include the Hebrew reference to "the Bow," and translates the Hebrew "Book of Jashar" as "the Book of the Upright."
notes.1:19: The Greek reads the imperative "Set up a monument" (Steloson), whereas the Hebrew reads "The gazelle" or "The beauty of Israel."
notes.1:20: The Greek uses "foreigners" (allophyloi), the Septuagint's standard designation for the Philistines throughout the books of Kingdoms.
notes.2:2: The Greek identifies Ahinoam as "the Israelitess" (Israeleitis), whereas the Hebrew reads "the Jezreelitess."
notes.2:5: The Greek reads "the mercy of God" (to eleos tou theou), where the Hebrew reads "this kindness."
notes.2:9: The Greek preserves the distinct name "Thasiri" and reads "Israel" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "the Ashurites" and "Jezreel."
notes.2:16: The Greek renders the Hebrew place name Helkath Hazzurim as "the Portion of the Plotters" (Meris ton epiboulon).
notes.2:29: The Greek renders three Hebrew geographic names descriptively: "toward the west" (for the Arabah), "the adjoining region" (for Bithron), and "the camp" (for Mahanaim).
notes.3:2: In verses 2–4, the Greek text preserves several distinct forms of proper names and gentilics: "the Israelitess" (MT "the Jezreelitess"), "Daluia" (MT "Chileab"), "Thommei" (MT "Talmai"), "Orneil" (MT "Adonijah"), and "Pheggith" (MT "Haggith").
notes.3:7: Throughout chapters 3–4, the Greek text names Saul's son "Mephibosheth" (where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Ish-bosheth"), and here calls Rizpah's father "Ial" (MT "Aiah").
notes.3:12: The Greek reads "at Thailam, where he was, at once," reflecting a double rendering of the Hebrew expression for "from where he was," and omits the question "Whose is the land?"
notes.3:33: The Greek renders the Hebrew word for "fool" (naval) as the proper name "Nabal" in verses 33–34, and in verse 34 reads "he did not draw near like Nabal" where the Hebrew reads "as one falls."
notes.3:39: The Greek reads "a kinsman and appointed by a king," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "weak, though anointed king."
notes.4:4: The Greek reads "from Israel" (where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "from Jezreel") and uses a masculine noun (tithenos) for Mephibosheth's nurse or attendant.
notes.4:6: The Greek preserves the narrative of the doorkeeper who grew drowsy while cleaning wheat so that the brothers slipped past unnoticed, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text describes them entering as though to fetch wheat.
notes.4:7: The Greek reads "the way toward the west," interpreting the Hebrew geographic term for the Jordan Valley (ha-arabah, "the Arabah") as "the west."
notes.5:6: The Greek states that the blind and the lame themselves stood in opposition, saying David would not enter, differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's taunt about removing them.
notes.5:8: The Greek reads "with a dagger" (en paraxiphidi) rather than the Hebrew "by the water shaft," and explicitly adds "of the Lord" after "house."
notes.5:13: The Greek text reads "after he came to Hebron" (eis Chebron) rather than "from Hebron" as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.5:16: The Greek preserves distinct forms of several names (such as Epidae and Eliphaath) and appends a second list of thirteen additional names of David's sons not present in the Hebrew text of 2 Samuel.
notes.5:17: Greek allophyloi ("foreigners") is the Septuagint's regular designation for the Philistines throughout Kingdoms; likewise, the Greek renders Rephaim as "the Titans" (5:18, 22) and Baal-perazim as "Upper Breaches" (5:20).
notes.6:1: The Greek reads "about seventy thousand" young men, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "thirty thousand" chosen men.
notes.6:3: The Greek uses singular verbs ("he placed... and carried"), reads "to the house of Amminadab" (Hebrew "from the house of Abinadab"), and translates Ahio as "his brothers."
notes.6:6: The Greek names the threshing floor "Nodab" (Hebrew "Nacon") and states that "the calf drew him aside" rather than that the oxen stumbled.
notes.6:10: The Greek reads "Abeddara" (Hebrew "Obed-edom") here and in 6:11–12, and includes "of the covenant" in "the ark of the covenant of the Lord."
notes.6:13: The Greek describes "seven choirs" bearing the ark with a calf and a lamb as a sacrifice, differing markedly from the Hebrew reading of "six steps" with an ox and a fattened animal.
notes.7:1: Greek κατεκληρονόμησεν literally means "gave him an inheritance," reflecting the Hebrew root for inheriting where the Masoretic Text reads "gave him rest."
notes.7:5: The Septuagint presents a direct prohibition ("You shall not build Me a house") rather than the rhetorical question found in the Masoretic Text.
notes.7:11: The Greek reads "that you shall build a house for Him," differing from the Masoretic Text ("that the LORD will make you a house"), though 7:27 in the Greek retains "I will build a house for you."
notes.7:15: The Septuagint omits Saul's name and reads broadly "from those whom I removed from before My face," and in 7:16 shifts to the third person ("his house... before Me").
notes.7:23: Greek σκηνώματα ("tents") stands where the Masoretic Text reads "its gods," and ἐπιφάνειαν ("glorious manifestation") translates the Hebrew for awesome deeds.
notes.8:1: Greek οἱ ἀλλόφυλοι ("foreigners") is the standard Septuagint term for the Philistines in Kingdoms, and τὴν ἀφωρισμένην ("the set-apart territory") translates the Hebrew place-name Metheg-ammah.
notes.8:2: The Septuagint specifies "the two lines" for those kept alive as well as those put to death, whereas the Masoretic Text has two lines put to death and one full line kept alive.
notes.8:7: Greek χλίδωνας means "bracelets" (for Masoretic "shields"). The closing clause about Shishak is a Septuagint addition that names "Jeroboam the son of Solomon" where 1 Kings 14:25 names Rehoboam.
notes.8:8: "Masbak" (Μασβὰκ) and "the choice cities" correspond to Betah and Berothai in the Masoretic Text; the closing clause about Solomon's bronze furnishings is a Septuagint addition parallel to 1 Chronicles 18:8.
notes.8:10: "Jedduran" (Ἰεδδουρὰν) is a distinct Septuagint form of the son's name (compare Joram in Masoretic 2 Samuel 8:10 and Hadoram in 1 Chronicles 18:10).
notes.8:13: "Gebelem" (Γεβέλεμ) is a Septuagint transliteration of the Hebrew for "Valley of Salt," and "Idumea" stands here and in 8:12 where the Masoretic Text reads Aram (Syria).
notes.8:18: In 8:16-18 the Septuagint has the distinct personal names Ahijah (for Ahilud), Asa (for Seraiah), and Janak (for Jehoiada); it also styles Benaiah as "counselor" (σύμβουλος) and David's sons as "chiefs of the court" (αὐλάρχαι, for Masoretic "priests").
notes.9:4: The Greek reads "Amaer" (Ἀμαὴρ) in 9:4, whereas 9:5 gives the standard form "Ammiel" (Ἀμειὴλ).
notes.9:7: The Septuagint explicitly reads "your father's father," clarifying Saul's relationship to Mephibosheth where the Masoretic Text simply reads "your father."
notes.9:11: The Septuagint presents the closing clause as third-person narrative ("And Mephibosheth ate at the table of David") rather than a continuation of David's direct speech.
notes.10:3: The Greek uses three verbs of reconnaissance ("search... spy it out... inspect it"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "overthrow it" for the third verb.
notes.10:4: The Greek states simply that Hanun shaved "their beards," without the word "half" found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.10:6: The Greek preserves several distinctive readings here: "the people of David had been put to shame" (MT: "had become odious to David"), "the king of Amalek" (MT: "king of Maacah"), and the proper name "Istob" (transliterating Hebrew Ish-tob, "men of Tob").
notes.10:16: The Greek names the river "Chalamak" (where the Hebrew Masoretic Text simply reads "the River," referring to the Euphrates) and uses the spelling "Hadarezer" rather than "Hadadezer."
notes.11:3: The Greek identifies Bathsheba's father as "Eliab," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Eliam."
notes.11:4: The Greek makes David the subject who "went in to her," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "she came to him."
notes.11:21: The Greek has the distinctive names "Jeroboam the son of Ner" (MT: "Jerubbesheth," another name for Jerubbaal/Gideon) and "Thamasi" (MT: "Thebez").
notes.11:22: The Greek contains a substantial expansion explicitly recounting David's angry rebuke to Joab's messenger, fulfilling Joab's prediction in verses 20-21; this portion is absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.12:6: The Greek text reads 'sevenfold' (heptaplasiona), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'fourfold.'
notes.12:21: The Greek text adds 'and kept vigil' and 'and drank,' details not present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.12:30: The Greek text preserves the distinct proper name 'Melchol' alongside 'their king,' whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has only 'their king' (or 'Milcom').
notes.13:15: The Greek text includes the clause 'the latter wickedness was greater than the first,' which is absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text and anticipates Tamar's words in verse sixteen.
notes.13:21: The Greek text includes 'yet he did not grieve the spirit of Amnon his son, because he loved him, for he was his firstborn,' a reading also supported at Qumran but absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.13:27: The Greek text adds the closing sentence 'And Absalom made a feast like the feast of the king,' which is absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.13:34: The Greek text adds the watchman's report to the king along with the distinct place name 'Oronen' (perhaps Horonaim or Beth-horon), which is absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.13:37: The Greek text reads the distinct form 'Tholmailem' (corresponding to Talmai in the Hebrew Masoretic Text) and adds the destination 'into Machad' (likely Maacah).
notes.13:39: The Greek verb ekopasen means 'ceased' or 'desisted' from going out against Absalom, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text is often translated 'longed.'
notes.14:14: The Greek lacks the negations found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, reading affirmatively that God will take a life while devising to banish one who is banished.
notes.14:17: The Greek reads 'for sacrifices' (thysias), reflecting Hebrew minchah ('offering') rather than menuchah ('rest, comfort').
notes.14:27: The Greek includes an additional notice that Tamar became the wife of Rehoboam the son of Solomon and bore him Abiathar (cf. Abijam/Abijah in 1 Kings 14:31; 15:1-2).
notes.15:12: The Greek calls Ahithophel 'the Tekonite' (rather than 'the Gilonite' as in the Hebrew) and reads 'a mighty calamity' (syntrimma, 'crushing, ruin') where the Hebrew has 'conspiracy'.
notes.15:18: The Greek preserves a doubled account of the procession, naming both the Hittites and the Cherethites, adding a stop by the olive tree in the wilderness, and reading 'to Gath' rather than 'from Gath'.
notes.15:19: The Greek spells the Gittite commander's name 'Setthei' here and in verse 22, and 'Etthei' (Ittai) in verse 21.
notes.15:24: The Greek adds the place name 'from Baithar' to the account of the Levites bearing the ark, a detail absent from the Hebrew text.
notes.15:28: The Greek transliterates the Hebrew word for 'plains' or 'steppes' as 'Araboth' and reads 'am encamped' (strateuomai) where the Hebrew has 'tarrying'.
notes.15:32: The Greek transliterates the Hebrew word for 'summit' (rosh) as the proper name 'Roos' and includes the title 'David's companion' for Hushai.
notes.16:1: The Greek transliterates the Hebrew word for the summit (ha-rosh) as the place name Ros, specifies dates (phoinikes) where the Hebrew has summer fruits, and uses the loanword nebel for the wine skin.
notes.16:16: The Greek records Hushai's acclamation once, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text repeats it twice.
notes.16:23: The Greek reads 'in those former days,' whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'in those days.'
notes.17:3: The Greek preserves the distinctive simile 'as a bride returns to her husband; you seek the life of only one man,' differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.17:8: The Greek includes the additional simile 'and like a fierce wild sow in the plain,' which is absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.17:16: The Greek transliterates the Hebrew word for plains as Araboth and reads katapeise ('prevail upon' or 'persuade'), where other witnesses and the Hebrew read 'swallow up.'
notes.17:25: The Greek calls Amasa's father Jether the Israelite and uses the masculine noun 'brother' (adelphou), making Nahash the brother of Zeruiah.
notes.17:27: The Greek fuses the Hebrew conjunction and name (we-Shobi) into the single name Uesbi, and in verses 28-29 adds 'ten' before both beds and basins while transliterating the Hebrew term for cattle cheeses as saphoth.
notes.18:13: The Greek links the opening infinitive clause ("so as not to do wrong against his life") as part of King David's command in verse 12, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text begins a new statement by the soldier.
notes.18:14: The Septuagint preserves Joab's distinctive opening clause ("I will begin this; I will not wait thus before you") and uses a plural verb ("they thrust them"), whereas the Hebrew has a singular verb.
notes.18:18: The Greek contains a distinctive doublet ("the pillar in which he was taken, and had erected it to take for himself") and reports Absalom's words in indirect speech; "the Hand of Absalom" literally renders the Greek name of the monument.
notes.18:23: "Kechar" follows the Greek transliteration of the Hebrew term for the Jordan Valley plain.
notes.18:28: The Greek reads "who hated their hand against my lord the king," reflecting a Hebrew textual variant ("hated") rather than the Masoretic Text's "lifted up."
notes.19:1: In the Septuagint (as in the Hebrew versification), David's lament over Absalom opens chapter nineteen rather than closing chapter eighteen, and the Greek places "my son, my son" twice before "Absalom."
notes.19:10: The Greek text regularly designates the Philistines as "foreigners" in First and Second Kingdoms, and here adds "and from his kingdom" to the account of David's flight.
notes.19:25: The Septuagint explicitly identifies Mephibosheth as "the son of the son of Saul" (Saul's grandson) and includes the additional detail that he had not pared his nails.
notes.19:44: The Septuagint includes the claim "and I am the firstborn rather than you," reflecting a longer reading absent from the Masoretic Text.
notes.20:6: The Greek reads "cast a shadow over our eyes," rendering the underlying Hebrew as derived from "shade" rather than "escape."
notes.20:14: The Septuagint reads "all who were in Charri" where the Masoretic Text refers to the Berites (or Bichrites).
notes.20:18: The Septuagint preserves a longer form of the ancient saying, referring to inquiry made in both Abel and Dan as to whether the customs established by the faithful of Israel had failed.
notes.20:23: The Greek text names "Benaiah the son of Ahilud" (sharing the patronymic of Jehoshaphat in verse twenty-four), whereas the Masoretic Text reads "son of Jehoiada."
notes.20:25: The Septuagint gives the scribe's name as "Joshua" (Greek Iesous), where the Masoretic Text reads "Sheva."
notes.21:2: The Greek reads "of the blood of the Amorites" (ek tou haimatos), a distinctive Septuagint reading where the Hebrew text has "of the remnant of the Amorites."
notes.21:8: The Greek text names Michal's husband Serei, where the Hebrew text reads Adriel.
notes.21:11: The closing sentence ("And they grew faint, and Dan the son of Joa, of the descendants of the giants, overtook them") is a distinctive Septuagint reading absent from the Hebrew text, anticipating the giant narratives in verses 15-22.
notes.21:14: "At the side" renders the Greek en te pleura, a literal translation of the Hebrew place name Zela ("rib" or "side"); similarly, verse 12 reads simply Baith rather than Beth-shan.
notes.21:19: The Greek preserves several distinctive proper names in verses 16-20, including Jesbi (v. 16), Oebocha the Hastatothite and Seph (v. 18), Rom, Ariorgim, and Godoliah the Hittite (v. 19, where the Hebrew has Gob, Jaare-oregim, and Goliath the Gittite), and Madon (v. 20).
notes.22:6: The Greek reads "of death" in both clauses and renders the second noun as "severities" (sklerotetes), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "cords of Sheol" and "snares of death."
notes.22:30: "Girded for action" translates the rare Greek adjective monozonos (literally "single-girded" or lightly armed for rapid combat), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to a raiding troop.
notes.22:32: The Greek calls God "Creator" (ktistes) rather than "Rock," reflecting a recurring Septuagint preference to avoid literal rock imagery for God (compare "guardian," phylax, in vv. 3 and 47).
notes.22:36: In this Greek text, "into a broad space for my steps beneath me" stands at the end of v. 36 rather than at the start of v. 37, and "Your attentiveness" (hypakoe) refers to God's gracious heeding of David's cry.
notes.22:51: The Greek text attaches the opening heading of the next section ("And these are the last words of David") to the end of 22:51 rather than placing it at the start of 23:1.
notes.23:1: The Greek opens with "Faithful is David" and "whom the Lord raised up over the anointed of the God of Jacob," differing from the Masoretic Text ("Now these are the last words of David... raised up on high").
notes.23:3: The Greek reads "Speak a parable: 'In man, how shall you strengthen the fear of the anointed?'" (Greek phobon christou), whereas the Masoretic Text speaks of one who rules justly in the fear of God.
notes.23:8: Throughout this roster of David's mighty men (including Jebosthe the Canaanite and Adinon the Asonite here, as well as numerous names in verses 25-38), the Greek preserves distinctive proper-name forms and places the displaced names of verse 30 into verse 37.
notes.23:13: The Greek reads the place name "Kadon" where the Masoretic Text has "at harvest time"; throughout this passage the Septuagint uses allophyloi ("foreigners") as its standard designation for the Philistines.
notes.24:5: Verses 5-7 preserve Septuagint-distinct place names: Aroel, Eliezer, Thabason (which is Nadasai), Dan Eidan and Oudan, and Mapsar of Tyre (a transliteration of the Hebrew term for "fortress").
notes.24:13: The Greek reads "three years of famine" (matching 1 Chronicles 21:12) rather than "seven years" as in the Masoretic Text, and uses thanatos ("death/pestilence") here and in verse 15.
notes.24:15: The Greek includes clauses not in the Masoretic Text ("David chose for himself the pestilence," "the days of the wheat harvest," and "the plague began among the people") and reads "until the hour of the midday meal" (Greek horas aristou).
notes.24:25: The Septuagint calls the Jebusite Orna (verses 16-24, corresponding to Araunah) and adds the historical note here that Solomon later enlarged the altar because it was small at first.
